              Write R=(r_1,r_2,...) and S=(s_1,s_2,...), with both components of order at least two as in same_end_extenders_initial_reversal01. In the no-order-disagreement branch, for each extender z∈{x,y} and each residual component U, failure of z to prepend U can occur only when the first two vertices of U lie in different displayed cores; boundary flip then gives a tight reverse cross triple through z.
              
              Form the bipartite graph B with left vertices {x,y}, right vertices {R,S}, and edge zU exactly when z can be prepended to U. If B had a perfect matching, assigning the two extenders to the matched residual components would produce two tight paths covering all of H, contrary to pc(H)>2. Hence B has no perfect matching.
              
              By Hall's theorem for this 2-by-2 graph, either some left vertex has empty neighborhood or some right vertex has empty neighborhood. In the first case one extender z fails to prepend both R and S; therefore both initial edges are cross-core and both boundary-reversed triples through z are tight. In the second case one residual component U is not prependable by either extender; therefore its initial edge is cross-core and its boundary reversals through x and y are both tight.
              
              This is strictly stronger than the existence of one reverse cross triple: the obstruction is synchronized either by a common reversing label or by a common reversed residual edge. No additional size assumptions are used.

            • [same_end_extenders_four_endpoint_reversal01] Universal same-end extenders force four synchronized endpoint reversals
                STATEMENT
                Let H be a boundary 3-tournament with pc(H)>2. Let A_1,...,A_q be pairwise vertex-disjoint tight paths of order at least two whose supports, together with distinct vertices x,y, partition V(H), and assume x and y both initial-extend every A_j. Let T=R|S be any exact two-cover of H-{x,y} having no order disagreement with any displayed A_j. Then one of the following holds. (I) One extender z in {x,y} cannot be attached to either end of either R or S; consequently the first and last ordinary edges of both R and S are cross-core and all four corresponding boundary-reversed endpoint triples through z are tight. (II) One residual component U in {R,S} cannot be extended at either end by either x or y; consequently both endpoint edges of U are cross-core and their four boundary-reversed triples through x and y are tight. The terminal-extender version is symmetric.
                BODY / PROOF
                For z in {x,y} and U in {R,S}, call z attachable to U if either prepending z to U or appending z to U gives a tight path. Form the bipartite attachment graph B with left class {x,y}, right class {R,S}, and edge zU exactly when z is attachable to U.
                
                If B has a perfect matching, attach the matched extender to the matched residual component at whichever end certifies that edge. The two resulting tight paths are vertex-disjoint and span H, contradicting pc(H)>2. Thus B has no perfect matching. Since B is 2-by-2, Hall's theorem says that either some extender z has no neighbor or some residual component U has no neighbor.
                
                It remains to translate a missing incidence zU. Write U=(u_1,...,u_m), m>=2. If z cannot be prepended, then (z,u_1,u_2) is non-tight. Boundary flip gives (u_2,u_1,z) tight. If u_1,u_2 lay in one displayed core A_j, the tight path (u_2,u_1,z) would place their common pair in the opposite relative order from A_j, contrary to the assumed absence of order disagreement. Hence u_1,u_2 lie in different displayed cores, and (u_2,u_1,z) is a reverse cross-core initial-end triple.
                
                Likewise, failure to append z means (u_{m-1},u_m,z) is non-tight, so boundary flip gives (z,u_m,u_{m-1}) tight. If u_{m-1},u_m belonged to one displayed core, this would reverse their common pair relative to that core and give order disagreement. Hence the terminal edge is cross-core and (z,u_m,u_{m-1}) is the corresponding reverse terminal-end triple.
                
                Therefore every missing incidence zU supplies two positioned reverse endpoint triples, one at each end of U. In Hall alternative (I), the two missing incidences zR,zS give four triples, one at each end of both residual components, all through the same extender z. In alternative (II), the two missing incidences xU,yU give four triples, both ends of one residual component reversed through both extenders. This proves the claim.
                
                The proof uses no size information beyond residual component order at least two and no local case analysis. It strictly strengthens the initial-end Hall obstruction by exploiting both endpoint attachment choices.

              • [same_end_extenders_hall_completion01] The four-endpoint Hall obstruction reduces to a shared-edge six-window or a same-deletion transfer fork
                  STATEMENT
                  Let H be a minimum counterexample in the setup of same_end_extenders_four_endpoint_reversal01, with universal same-end extenders x,y and an order-neutral exact residual two-cover T=R|S of H-{x,y}. Then either one residual component is unattached at either end by both x and y, in which case the two labels reverse one common displayed endpoint edge and shared_edge_double_reversal_sixpackage01 gives its common-core six-window transport package; or, after relabeling the extenders z,w, z is unattached at either end of both R and S while w is attachable to both. In the latter case H-z has two exact two-covers obtained by attaching w to R or to S, their singleton lifts are adjacent three-covers, and singleton_transfer_endpointization01 yields either a displayed component-end reversal or coherent same-end endpoint alignment of w on both augmented residual supports.
                  BODY / PROOF
                  Form the 2-by-2 bipartite attachment graph B with left class {x,y}, right class {R,S}, and edge tU when t can be attached to at least one end of U. A perfect matching would attach the two extenders to different residual paths and give a spanning two-cover of H, so B has no perfect matching. If some right vertex U has degree zero, then both extenders fail to attach at either end of U. By same_end_extenders_four_endpoint_reversal01, each endpoint edge of U is reversed through both x and y. Choosing either endpoint edge gives two labels reversing one common displayed path edge, so shared_edge_double_reversal_sixpackage01 applies. Now assume no right vertex is isolated. Since B has no perfect matching, Hall's theorem for this 2-by-2 graph gives an isolated left vertex z; let w be the other extender. Every right vertex has a neighbor and z has none, hence w is adjacent to both R and S. Choose endpoint attachments certifying those incidences. Attaching w to R gives an exact two-cover (R+w)|S of H-z, while attaching w to S gives R|(S+w). Adjoining the singleton {z} gives two spanning three-covers of H differing by one legal pairwise repartition on R union S union {w}. Apply singleton_transfer_endpointization01 to the transferred label w and unchanged third component {z}. Opposite endpoint realizations produce a displayed component-end reversal. Otherwise that theorem leaves universal internality on one augmented support or coherent same-end alignment. Universal internality is impossible because w is explicitly attachable to both residual paths, so in the no-reversal branch every endpoint realization of w is initial on both augmented supports or terminal on both.

                • [blocked_extender_coherent_sameend_escape01] A blocked extender opposite a coherent mobile extender reduces to a five-window, doubled barrier, or six-window package
                    STATEMENT
                    Let H be a minimum counterexample and let R=(r_1,...,r_m), S=(s_1,...,s_l), with m,l>=2, be an exact two-cover of H-{z,w}. Suppose z cannot be attached to either end of either R or S, while w initial-extends both R and S. Then at least one of the following occurs: (1) H has a proper Hamiltonian five-set with non-Hamiltonian path-cover-two complement; (2) both (w,s_1,r_1) and (w,r_1,s_1) are tight, giving a doubled reverse-end barrier; (3) two labels reverse the same terminal edge of the two-path (w,z), and the resulting pair of reversal triples forces two Hamiltonian five-sets with a common four-core and hence the six-window transport package of yield_a_hamiltonian_sixset_or_fourgooddeletion_transport. The terminal-extension version is symmetric.
                    BODY / PROOF
                    Because (w,R)|S is an exact two-cover of H-z, the omitted vertex z cannot prepend to the displayed path (w,R); otherwise (z,w,R)|S would be a spanning two-cover of H. Thus (z,w,r_1) is non-tight, and boundary antisymmetry gives (r_1,w,z) tight. Similarly (s_1,w,z) is tight. Hence r_1 and s_1 are two same-end initial extenders of the two-vertex path Q=(w,z). If some vertex c outside {w,z,r_1,s_1} terminal-extends Q, so (w,z,c) is tight, apply extenders_force_hamiltonicity_or_two_reverse_endpoint_triples to Q with the two initial extenders r_1,s_1 and the terminal extender c. It yields either a Hamiltonian path on the five-set {w,z,r_1,s_1,c}, which is proper and therefore has a non-Hamiltonian path-cover-two complement, or the doubled reverse triples (w,s_1,r_1) and (w,r_1,s_1). This gives (1) or (2). Assume instead that no such c terminal-extends Q. Then for every c outside {w,z,r_1,s_1}, (w,z,c) is non-tight and hence (c,z,w) is tight. Since a minimum counterexample has order greater than ten, choose distinct c,d outside {w,z,r_1,s_1}. The triples T_c=(c,z,w) and T_d=(d,z,w) are genuine terminal reversals of the same displayed edge. Apply reversal_dense_fivefamily01 to each. On the common outside vertex set, the graph of pairs that fail to Hamiltonize T_c is triangle-free, and the analogous bad graph for T_d is triangle-free. If no pair Hamiltonized both reversal triples, the complete graph on any six common outside vertices could be two-colored by assigning every pair to one of the two bad graphs, with neither color containing a triangle. The elementary K_6 triangle argument rules this out. Hence some pair a,b Hamiltonizes both five-sets {c,z,w,a,b} and {d,z,w,a,b}. These share the four-core {z,w,a,b}, so yield_a_hamiltonian_sixset_or_fourgooddeletion_transport gives the stated six-window transport package. The case where w terminal-extends both R and S is obtained by reversing the end roles throughout.

              • [unique_small_four_endpoint_reversal01] The witness-free unique-small equitable residue forces four synchronized endpoint reversals
                  STATEMENT
                  Let H be a minimum counterexample and let K be a trapped pairwise-repartition component at minimum quadratic potential in which every three-cover has path-order multiset {r+1,r+1,r}, r>=3. Assume none of the canonical terminal-frontier witnesses excluded in unique_small_transport_recomp02 occurs. Then there are distinct vertices x,y and an exact two-cover T=R|S of H-{x,y} such that, after possibly reversing the global displayed orientation, either one extender z in {x,y} reverses both endpoint edges of both R and S, or one residual component U in {R,S} has both endpoint edges reversed through both x and y. In all four instances the reversed endpoint edge is cross-core relative to the three order-r displayed cores.
                  BODY / PROOF
                  The witness-free unique-small theorem unique_small_transport_recomp02 provides three disjoint order-r core paths A,B,C and distinct exterior vertices x,y which both extend the same end of every core. Reverse the global displayed orientation if necessary so that both are initial extenders.
                  
                  By minimum-counterexample minimality, H-{x,y} has path-cover number at most two. It cannot be Hamiltonian, since a Hamilton path on H-{x,y} together with the two-vertex path (x,y) would two-cover H. Hence choose an exact two-cover T=R|S. The witness-free hypothesis excludes relative-order disagreement between T and the displayed cores.
                  
                  Apply same_end_extenders_four_endpoint_reversal01. Its first Hall alternative gives one extender z which is unattached at either end of either residual component, and hence four reverse cross-core endpoint triples through z. Its second alternative gives one residual component U to which neither x nor y attaches at either end, and hence four reverse cross-core endpoint triples, through both extenders at both ends of U. This proves the stated normal form.

            • [unique_small_double_reversal01] The witness-free unique-small equitable residue forces synchronized double endpoint reversal
                STATEMENT
                Let H be a minimum counterexample and let K be a trapped pairwise-repartition component at minimum quadratic potential in which every three-cover has path-order multiset {r+1,r+1,r}, r>=3. Assume none of the canonical terminal-frontier witnesses excluded in unique_small_transport_recomp02 occurs. Then there are distinct vertices x,y and a two-cover T=R|S of H-{x,y} such that, after possibly reversing the global displayed orientation, either one of x,y reverses the initial edge of both R and S, or one of R,S has an initial edge whose boundary reversal is tight through both x and y. Thus the witness-free unique-small equitable residue forces a synchronized double endpoint-reversal obstruction.
                BODY / PROOF
                By unique_small_transport_recomp02, the witness-free unique-small branch yields disjoint tight core paths A,B,C of order r and distinct exterior vertices x,y such that x and y both initial-extend each of A,B,C, after globally reversing the displayed orientations if necessary.
                
                Because H is a minimum counterexample, the proper induced subtournament H-{x,y} has path-cover number at most two. It is not Hamiltonian: otherwise a Hamilton path on H-{x,y}, together with the two-vertex tight path (x,y), would two-cover H. Hence choose an exact two-cover T=R|S of H-{x,y}.
                
                The witness-free hypotheses exclude relative-order disagreement with the displayed cores. Apply same_end_extenders_double_reversal01 to A,B,C,x,y and T. Its Hall obstruction gives exactly one of the following: one extender z in {x,y} cannot be prepended to either R or S, so both residual initial edges are cross-core and their boundary reversals through z are tight; or one residual component U in {R,S} cannot be prepended by either extender, so its cross-core initial edge has tight boundary reversals through both x and y.
                
                This yields the asserted synchronized double endpoint reversal. In particular the older four-way crossing taxonomy from unique_small_transport_recomp02 is not needed as the terminal description of the witness-free unique-small branch.

          • [unique_small_endpoint_reversal01] The witness-free unique-small quadratic residue enters endpoint reversal
              STATEMENT
              Let H be a minimum counterexample and let K be a trapped pairwise-repartition component at minimum quadratic potential in which every three-cover has path-order multiset {r+1,r+1,r}, r>=3. Assume none of the canonical terminal-frontier witnesses listed in unique_small_transport_recomp02 occurs. Then H contains a tight path R=(u,v,...) and a vertex z outside R such that (v,u,z) is tight. Thus the unique-small neutral residue contains a literal initial-edge reversal and enters the certified endpoint-reversal machinery directly.
              BODY / PROOF
              By unique_small_transport_recomp02, the witness-free hypotheses yield disjoint tight paths A,B,C of order r and distinct vertices x,y outside them such that x and y both extend the same endpoint of all three cores. Reverse the global notation if needed and assume they both initial-extend A,B,C.
              
              Because H is a minimum counterexample, the proper induced subtournament H-{x,y} has path-cover number at most two. If it were Hamiltonian, a Hamilton path on H-{x,y} together with the two-vertex path (x,y) would be a spanning two-cover of H, impossible. Hence choose a two-cover T of H-{x,y}; it has two nonempty components.
              
              Apply same_end_extenders_initial_reversal01 to A,B,C,x,y and T. That theorem gives either order disagreement between T and one displayed core, or a component R=(u,v,...) of T whose first two vertices lie in different cores and a label z in {x,y} for which (v,u,z) is tight.
              
              The first alternative is excluded by the witness-free hypothesis of unique_small_transport_recomp02. Therefore the second alternative holds. Since R is a tight path and z is outside R, the tight triple (v,u,z) reverses the displayed initial edge (u,v) of R in the literal sense used by the endpoint-reversal classification. No crossing-count case analysis is required.
              
              Consequently the former unique-small four-way comparison-cover residue can be replaced, for theorem-facing purposes, by direct entry into endpoint_reversal_obstruction_recomp01 and its descendants. This does not by itself close the grand theorem: the endpoint-reversal chain can still return bounded order disagreement or other canonical local disturbances. It does, however, eliminate crossing multiplicity, inherited-core separation, and leave-and-return as necessary terminal descriptions of this particular neutral branch.

        • [under_universal_initial_extenders_forces_a_fourwindow] A two-crossing leave-return under universal initial extenders forces a four-window
            STATEMENT
            Let H be a minimum counterexample. Let A,B,C be disjoint displayed tight paths of a common order r>=3, and let x,y be distinct vertices outside them such that both x and y initial-extend each of A,B,C.
            
            Suppose a two-cover T of H-{x,y}=A union B union C is order-neutral on each displayed core and has exactly two cross-core edges. Suppose one T-component has leave-and-return form
            A_1, D, A_2,
            where A=A_1 A_2 is the displayed A-order split into two nonempty contiguous blocks, D is one of the whole cores B,C in its displayed order, and the other T-component is the remaining whole core E.
            
            Then either H has a spanning two-cover, or H contains a proper Hamiltonian four-set W whose complement is non-Hamiltonian with path-cover number two.
            
            Consequently, in the witness-free unique-small plateau of unique_small_transport_recomp02, the two-crossing leave-and-return alternative cannot occur.
            BODY / PROOF
            Because T has exactly two cross-core edges, its four maximal core blocks have counts 2,1,1. Hence in the stated leave-and-return case the intervening block D is an entire core and the other component E is the remaining entire core.
            
            Write A_1=(a_1,...,a_t) in the inherited order. If t>=2, then x initial-extends A, so (x,a_1,a_2) is tight. Prepending x to the T-component A_1,D,A_2 therefore creates a tight path, while (y,E) is tight because y initial-extends E. These two paths would span H, impossible. Thus t=1.
            
            Write A_1=(a), D=(d_1,...,d_r), and let c be the first vertex of A_2. The T-component (a,D,A_2) shows that (a,D) and (D,c) are tight paths.
            
            If either (x,a,d_1) or (a,x,d_1) were tight, then respectively (x,a,D,A_2) or (a,x,D,A_2) would be a tight path, using the initial-extension property at the next new triple and inherited triples thereafter. Together with (y,E) this would two-cover H. Hence both are non-tight, so boundary reversal antisymmetry gives (d_1,a,x) and (d_1,x,a) tight. Exchanging x and y gives (d_1,a,y) and (d_1,y,a) tight.
            
            Now boundary reversal antisymmetry gives exactly one of (x,a,y) and (y,a,x) as tight. If (x,a,y) is tight, then (d_1,x,a,y) is a Hamilton tight path on W={d_1,a,x,y}, using (d_1,x,a). If (y,a,x) is tight, then (d_1,y,a,x) is a Hamilton tight path, using (d_1,y,a). Thus W is Hamiltonian without any four-vertex classification.
            
            The set W is proper because |V(H)|>=11. If H-W were Hamiltonian, Hamilton paths on W and H-W would two-cover H. Hence H-W is non-Hamiltonian, and minimum-counterexample calculus gives path-cover number two.
            
            Therefore the leave-and-return case yields either a spanning two-cover or the stated proper Hamiltonian four-set with path-cover-two complement.

        • [unique_small_bounded_endgame01] The unique-small quadratic plateau reduces to a positioned endpoint reversal or doubled reverse barrier
            STATEMENT
            Let H be a minimum counterexample and let K be a trapped pairwise-repartition component at minimum quadratic potential in which every three-cover has path-order multiset {r+1,r+1,r}, r>=3. Assume the canonical terminal-frontier outputs excluded in unique_small_transport_recomp02 have not already been accepted as the route output. Then the residual same-end neutral-transfer branch can be sharpened as follows: either it produces a positioned component-end reversal, or it produces a doubled reverse-end barrier. More precisely, the common-reversed-edge Hall branch produces two Hamiltonian five-sets with a common four-core and hence the complete square/overlap/matching-block six-shell normal form; in the complementary Hall branch there are two exact covers of one deletion differing by one transferred label, and endpointization gives a component-end reversal unless the moving label is coherently same-end on both residual paths; that coherent subcase yields a Hamiltonian five-window, the same common-core six-shell normal form, or a doubled reverse-end barrier. Thus, after exporting the already-standard Hamiltonian-window/six-shell outputs, the only new bounded residues of the unique-small plateau are endpoint reversal and doubled reverse barrier.
            BODY / PROOF
            Use unique_small_transport_recomp02 to obtain the universal same-end extender configuration and choose an exact residual two-cover with no relative-order disagreement in the residual branch under consideration. Apply same_end_extenders_hall_completion01. If one residual component is unattached by both extenders, the two extenders reverse one common displayed endpoint edge; shared_edge_double_reversal_sixpackage01 produces two Hamiltonian five-sets sharing a four-core, and commoncore_fivepair_sixshell_normal01 refines their union into the complete full-square / adjacent-overlap / oriented-matching-block six-shell menu. Otherwise Hall gives one blocked extender z and one mobile extender w attachable to both residual paths. The two resulting exact covers of H-z differ by moving w between those paths. singleton_transfer_endpointization01 gives a displayed component-end reversal unless the endpoint realizations of w are coherently same-end on both supports. In the coherent case apply blocked_extender_coherent_sameend_escape01. Its first outcome is a Hamiltonian five-window; its third outcome again gives two common-four-core Hamiltonian five-sets and therefore the six-shell normal form; its only remaining outcome is a doubled reverse-end barrier. These alternatives exhaust the residual same-end branch. The theorem deliberately does not claim that the doubled barrier itself is consumed: certified barrier-propagation results show it is a real endpoint-transport frontier, and generic local absorption is not presently established.

    • [every_onecrossing_residue_to_joinadjacent_insertion_gaps] Opposite donor endpoints localize every one-crossing residue to join-adjacent insertion gaps
        STATEMENT
        Let H be a minimum counterexample and let A=(x,M,y), B=(b_1,...,b_r), C=(c_1,...,c_r) be a Phi-minimal trapped three-cover with |A|=r+1, |B|=|C|=r and r>=3, so |M|=r-1. Suppose H[B+x] and H[C+y] are Hamiltonian while H[B+y] and H[C+x] are non-Hamiltonian. Assume Hamilton orders on B+x and C+y preserve the displayed relative orders of B and C, so x and y have successful insertion gaps in B and C respectively. Let T be a two-cover of H-{x,y}. Then either T has order disagreement with M,B, or C; or T has at least two ordinary edges joining distinct members of V(M)|V(B)|V(C); or T has exactly one such edge and, after possibly interchanging (x,B) with (y,C), one of the following holds: (i) B is an entire T-component, the other component is M followed by C, and every successful insertion gap of y in C is one of the first two gaps; (ii) M is an entire T-component, the other component is B followed by C, every successful insertion gap of x in B is one of the last two gaps, and every successful insertion gap of y in C is one of the first two gaps. The reversed concatenation C followed by B gives the mirror last-two/first-two conclusion. Thus the opposite-donor branch is either already a standard transport disturbance or is confined to endpoint-adjacent geometry at the unique core-core join.
        BODY / PROOF
        Count ordinary T-edges crossing the partition V(M)|V(B)|V(C). Component drop gives at least one. If there are at least two, the second outcome holds. Suppose there is exactly one and no order disagreement. Cutting that edge leaves exactly three monochromatic blocks, so each of M,B,C is one whole T-block in its displayed order; one block is an entire T-component and the other two are concatenated in one of the two possible orders. First suppose B is isolated. Replace B by a Hamilton path on B+x. If the other T-component were C followed by M, then appending y to M would give the tight path C,M,y because (M,y) is inherited from A, and together with B+x this would two-cover H. Hence the other component must be M followed by C. If y had any successful insertion gap in C other than the first two gaps, inserting y there would leave the first two vertices of C unchanged, so both join triples from M into C would remain tight; M followed by that enlarged C-path, together with B+x, would again two-cover H. Hence every successful gap of y in C is among the first two. The case C isolated is symmetric: the other component must be B followed by M, and every successful gap of x in B is among the last two. Finally suppose M is isolated. If the other component is B followed by C, then using the tight path (M,y) on the isolated support shows that any insertion of x into B outside the last two gaps would preserve the B-to-C join and give a two-cover; hence x is confined to the last two B-gaps. Using (x,M) on the isolated support similarly shows that y is confined to the first two C-gaps. If the concatenation is C followed by B the conclusions reverse. These are all possibilities.

      • [oppositedonor_residue_forces_a_reverse_cross_triple] Every join-adjacent opposite-donor residue forces a reverse cross triple
          STATEMENT
          Under the one-crossing join-adjacent alternatives of d4e6e9fba9ed, H necessarily contains an explicit tight triple obtained by reversing a failed new join triple. More precisely, if B is isolated and the other path is M followed by C, with m the terminal vertex of M, then insertion of y before c_1 forces (c_1,y,m) tight, while insertion of y between c_1,c_2 forces (y,c_1,m) tight. The case C isolated is symmetric. If M is isolated and the other path is B followed by C, then after inserting x in one of the last two B-gaps and y in one of the first two C-gaps, at least one of the two consecutive triples straddling the enlarged B-C join is non-tight, so its reversal is tight. Thus every one-crossing opposite-donor residue supplies a bounded reverse cross triple.
          BODY / PROOF
          Suppose first that B is an entire component of T and the other T-component is M followed by C. Replace B by any Hamilton path on B+x. By d4e6e9fba9ed, y inserts into C only in gap 0 or gap 1. If y inserts in gap 0, consider the sequence M,y,c_1,...,c_r. All consecutive triples are tight except possibly (m,y,c_1): the triple ending M with y is inherited from A=(x,M,y), and the triples from y onward belong to the successful insertion order. If (m,y,c_1) were tight, this path together with B+x would two-cover H. Hence it is non-tight and (c_1,y,m) is tight. If y inserts in gap 1, use M,c_1,y,c_2,...,c_r. The only possibly new triple is (m,c_1,y), so its failure is forced and (y,c_1,m) is tight. The case C isolated is symmetric: if T has B followed by M and x inserts after b_r, the only new triple is (b_r,x,m_1), forcing (m_1,x,b_r); if x inserts between b_{r-1},b_r, the only new triple is (x,b_r,m_1), forcing (m_1,b_r,x). Finally suppose M is isolated and T has B followed by C. Use a Hamilton path on M+x or M+y for the isolated component only to establish the localization from d4e6e9fba9ed; now simultaneously insert x into its permitted last-two gap of B and y into its permitted first-two gap of C in the concatenated B-C path. Every triple wholly inside the enlarged B-order or enlarged C-order is tight. Exactly two consecutive triples can be new at their join. If both were tight, the enlarged B-C sequence together with M would be a spanning two-cover of H. Therefore at least one is non-tight, and boundary antisymmetry makes its reversal tight. The C-followed-by-B case is identical with left and right interchanged.

      • [oppositedonor_residue_uses_the_unique_inner_joinadjacent_gaps] A witness-free one-crossing opposite-donor residue uses the unique inner join-adjacent gaps
          STATEMENT
          Continue the opposite-donor one-crossing residue of d4e6e9fba9ed, and assume in addition that no explicit cross triple is allowed. Then any successful insertion that d4e6e9fba9ed confines to the first two gaps is forced into gap 1 rather than the endpoint gap 0, and any successful insertion that it confines to the last two gaps is forced into gap r-1 rather than endpoint gap r. Thus every join-adjacent successful insertion in the one-crossing residue lies exactly one gap inward from the relevant core-core join.
          BODY / PROOF
          Suppose d4e6e9fba9ed confines y to the first two gaps of C=(c_1,...,c_r), while the inherited interior path M ends immediately before C in the one-crossing two-cover and (M,y) is tight as inherited from A=(x,M,y). If y used endpoint gap 0, then (y,c_1,c_2) is tight. Consider M,y,C. Every consecutive triple is already tight except possibly (m_last,y,c_1), where m_last is the final vertex of M. If that triple is tight, M,y,C together with the disjoint Hamilton path on B+x gives a spanning two-cover of H. If it is non-tight, boundary antisymmetry gives the explicit reverse cross triple (c_1,y,m_last). Both alternatives are excluded in the witness-free branch, so y cannot use gap 0; hence its confined successful gap is exactly gap 1. The last-gap assertion is symmetric. Namely, whenever d4e6e9fba9ed confines x to the last two gaps of B=(b_1,...,b_r) and the corresponding one-crossing geometry places B immediately before M with (x,M) inherited from A, using endpoint gap r makes B,x tight. The concatenation B,x,M then has only the possibly new join triple (b_r,x,m_1). If it is tight, B,x,M together with the disjoint Hamilton path on C+y gives a spanning two-cover; if it is non-tight, the reverse cross triple (m_1,x,b_r) is tight. Hence gap r is excluded and the confined successful gap is exactly gap r-1. No assertion is made about the successful insertion on an isolated core when d4e6e9fba9ed does not confine its gap.

    • [profile_always_exposes_a_standard_transport_disturbance] The unique-large equitable profile always exposes a standard transport disturbance
        STATEMENT
        Let H be a minimum counterexample and let A|B|C be a Phi-minimal trapped three-cover with |A|=r+1 and |B|=|C|=r, r>=3. Then at least one canonical terminal-frontier witness occurs, or the neutral-transfer residue exposes one of the standard endpoint-transport / defect-compression inputs: order disagreement, at least three ordinary comparison-cover edges crossing a displayed three-part core partition, an inherited displayed-core edge whose endpoints lie in different comparison-cover components, a leave-and-return excursion through another displayed core, or an explicit bounded reverse cross triple. Thus the nonuniform equitable profile {r+1,r,r} has no remaining structureless neutral-transfer branch.
        BODY / PROOF
        Write the endpoints of A as x,y. Apply the certified size-gap-one dichotomy to A|B and A|C. If either pair has no Hamiltonian endpoint enlargement, the paired-noninsertion branch and the universal two-noninsertable-vertex theorem already yield a canonical terminal-frontier witness. Hence assume each smaller path has at least one Hamiltonian enlargement by an endpoint of A. If the same endpoint, say x, Hamiltonizes both B+x and C+x, apply b5150f71d277: every two-cover of H-x has at least two edges crossing the equal-core partition (A-x)|B|C, and the transition-count equality case yields an inherited-core crossing or leave-and-return excursion, while three or more crossings give crossing multiplicity. Now suppose no endpoint Hamiltonizes both smaller paths. Since there are only the two endpoints x,y, after relabeling we have B+x and C+y Hamiltonian while B+y and C+x are non-Hamiltonian. If a chosen Hamilton order on B+x or C+y disagrees with the displayed order of its core, we have order disagreement. Otherwise x and y are successful insertions into B and C. Take a two-cover T of H-{x,y}. If T has order disagreement, we are done. If at least two T-edges cross the residual core partition M|B|C, where A=(x,M,y), then t>=3 gives crossing multiplicity and t=2 gives, by the transition-count argument, an inherited-core crossing or leave-and-return excursion. If t=1, d4e6e9fba9ed localizes the successful insertions to the two gaps adjacent to the unique core-core join, and f5a0b71835ae shows that attempting the corresponding enlarged concatenation forces an explicit reverse cross triple. These cases exhaust the two endpoint-enlargement sets for B and C.

    • [quadratic_minima_have_no_structureless_neutraltransfer_residue] Terminal quadratic minima have no structureless neutral-transfer residue
        STATEMENT
        Let H be a minimum counterexample and let C be a three-cover minimizing the quadratic potential in a trapped connected component of the pairwise-repartition graph. Then H exposes a canonical theorem-closure input: a proper Hamiltonian four- or five-vertex support with path-cover-two complement; an explicit cross triple or interval connector; order disagreement; an inherited displayed-path edge whose endpoints are separated by a comparison cover; a leave-and-return excursion through another displayed core; crossing multiplicity at least three; a bounded local defect-compression obstruction; or a reversed join. In particular, the neutral endpoint-transfer alternative of terminalfrontier_recomp01 never remains structureless.
        BODY / PROOF
        Apply terminalfrontier_recomp01. Every size-gap-at-least-two branch and the all-equal branch already yields one of the listed canonical inputs, so only the neutral size-gap-one branch needs attention. Because any pair of component orders differing by at least two was already handled, a nonuniform remaining size multiset has one of the two forms {r+1,r+1,r} or {r+1,r,r}. In the unique-small form {r+1,r+1,r}, the certified/pending sequential reduction ending at 7004825df9bf converts a witness-free neutral cycle into order disagreement, crossing multiplicity, an inherited-core crossing, or a leave-and-return excursion. In the unique-large form {r+1,r,r}, 939a6dc97467 gives the same conclusion or an explicit bounded reverse cross triple: if one endpoint of the large path transfers into both smaller paths, b5150f71d277 supplies the crossing disturbance after deleting that endpoint; otherwise the two smaller paths use opposite donor endpoints, d4e6e9fba9ed localizes any one-crossing two-deletion cover to join-adjacent insertion gaps, and f5a0b71835ae forces a reverse cross triple. Thus every neutral-transfer residue is converted to one of the listed canonical inputs.

    • [the_uniquelarge_profile_forces_a_standard_transport_disturbance] A common donor endpoint in the unique-large profile forces a standard transport disturbance
        STATEMENT
        Let H be a minimum counterexample and let A|B|C be a Phi-minimal trapped three-cover with |A|=r+1 and |B|=|C|=r, r>=3. Suppose one endpoint x of A has Hamiltonian enlargements H[V(B) union {x}] and H[V(C) union {x}]. Put A0=A-x with its inherited tight order. Then every two-cover T of H-x contains at least two ordinary path edges whose endpoints lie in different members of V(A0)|V(B)|V(C). Consequently T exposes crossing multiplicity, or in the two-crossing equality case an inherited-core crossing or a leave-and-return excursion. Thus the common-donor subcase of the unique-large profile reduces to the standard endpoint-transport / defect-compression inputs, with no assumption on the insertion positions of x in B or C.
        BODY / PROOF
        The paths A0,B,C are disjoint tight paths of the same order r. Moreover each of the three supports V(A0),V(B),V(C) becomes Hamiltonian after adjoining x: V(A0) union {x}=V(A) is Hamiltonian by the displayed path A, while the other two Hamiltonian enlargements are hypotheses. Let T be any two-cover of H-x, and let t be the number of ordinary T-edges joining distinct classes of the partition V(A0)|V(B)|V(C). The transition-count identity gives t>=1. Suppose t=1. Cutting the unique crossing edge leaves three monochromatic path blocks, one in each core. Since T has two path components, one of these three core blocks is itself an entire component of T; call its support D. The equality t=1 also forces that block to contain all vertices of its core. But H[D union {x}] is Hamiltonian. Replacing this entire component of T by a Hamilton path on D union {x}, while leaving the other component of T unchanged, gives a spanning two-cover of H, contradiction. Hence t>=2 for every T. If t>=3, crossing multiplicity is explicit. If t=2, cutting the two crossing edges produces four monochromatic blocks, so the three core block counts are (2,1,1). For the split core, either its two blocks lie in different T-components, in which case connectivity of the displayed core path gives an inherited core edge with endpoints in different T-components, or they lie in the same T-component separated by a nonempty block from another core, giving a leave-and-return excursion. These are standard transport-disturbance inputs.

      • [is_a_crossed_pair_of_onesuccess_onefailure_insertion_windows] The remaining unique-large residue is a crossed pair of one-success one-failure insertion windows
          STATEMENT
          Let H be a minimum counterexample and let A=(a_0,...,a_r)|B|C be a Phi-minimal trapped three-cover with |A|=r+1 and |B|=|C|=r, r>=3. Assume none of the canonical terminal-frontier witnesses occurs and assume the common-donor branch of b5150f71d277 does not occur. Then, after possibly interchanging B,C and reversing A, H[V(B) union {a_0}] and H[V(C) union {a_r}] are Hamiltonian, while H[V(B) union {a_r}] and H[V(C) union {a_0}] are non-Hamiltonian. In the no-order-disagreement branch, a_0 has a unique successful insertion position in the displayed order of B and a_r has a unique successful insertion position in the displayed order of C. The opposite labels a_r on B and a_0 on C are noninsertable and each satisfies one of the bounded failed-insertion normal forms of insert01. Moreover H-V(a_1,...,a_{r-1}) has the balanced two-cover (B+a_0)|(C+a_r).
          BODY / PROOF
          Apply the certified size-gap-one dichotomy 885fe451cb03 to A|B and A|C. Since the paired-noninsertion alternative would already give a terminal-frontier witness, each pair admits at least one endpoint transfer. For each recipient D in {B,C}, let S_D subseteq {a_0,a_r} be the nonempty set of donor endpoints whose enlargement D+x is Hamiltonian. If S_B and S_C intersect, the common-donor theorem b5150f71d277 applies, contrary to the present branch. Hence S_B and S_C are disjoint nonempty subsets of a two-element set; therefore, after relabeling, S_B={a_0} and S_C={a_r}. Thus B+a_0 and C+a_r are Hamiltonian, whereas B+a_r and C+a_0 are non-Hamiltonian. Outside relative-order disagreement, every Hamilton path on B+a_0 preserves the displayed B-order and is therefore obtained by inserting a_0 into that order. If there were two successful insertion positions, astra003uniqueinsertgap would itself give relative-order disagreement; hence the position is unique. The same holds for a_r in C. Since B+a_r is non-Hamiltonian, a_r is noninsertable into the displayed order of B, and insert01 supplies a bounded failed-insertion normal form; symmetrically a_0 is noninsertable into C with its own bounded obstruction. Finally B+a_0 and C+a_r are disjoint Hamiltonian supports whose union is V(H)-V(a_1,...,a_{r-1}), yielding the displayed balanced two-cover of the complement of the inherited interior path.

  • [to_descent_nearby_migration_or_an_endpointaligned_small_support] Four-window transport compresses to descent, nearby migration, or an endpoint-aligned small support
      STATEMENT
      Let H be a minimum counterexample, let W be a Hamiltonian four-set, and let H-W=P|Q be a two-cover. Then at least one of the following holds.
      
      (1) |V(H)|<=14.
      
      (2) The anchored three-cover W|P|Q admits an endpoint-transfer repartition of strictly smaller quadratic potential.
      
      (3) The bounded transport alternative of four_window_transport15 occurs: there are a three-set D, one displayed endpoint e of one complementary path, and both displayed endpoints f,g of the other such that D union {e,f} and D union {e,g} are Hamiltonian five-sets, with the associated six-set carrying the one- and two-label path-cover-two transport data of four_window_transport_allorders01. Moreover this branch can always be sharpened further to one of:
        (3a) a Hamiltonian four-set W1 with non-Hamiltonian path-cover-two complement and |W intersect W1|=3; or
        (3b) an endpoint-aligned small support: either a Hamiltonian four-set Z containing e,f,g with non-Hamiltonian path-cover-two complement, or a Hamiltonian five-set S with non-Hamiltonian path-cover-two complement and a Hamilton path whose two endpoints both lie in {e,f,g}.
      
      Thus above order fourteen an anchored Hamiltonian four-window cannot terminate in an unstructured order-disagreement residue: it either descends, moves to a distance-one four-window, or produces an explicitly endpoint-aligned Hamiltonian support of order four or five.
      BODY / PROOF
      Apply four_window_transport15. Its small-order and strict endpoint-transfer outcomes give (1) and (2), while its remaining outcome is exactly the bounded six-vertex transport package recorded in four_window_transport_allorders01.
      
      In that bounded branch, apply the shared-endpoint fork compression used in migration_is_distanceone_or_a_paired_oppositeend_fork. If one of the three one-endpoint replacements is Hamiltonian, minimum-counterexample calculus gives a Hamiltonian four-set W1 at Johnson distance one from W whose complement is non-Hamiltonian with path-cover number two, giving (3a). Otherwise two Hamiltonian four-windows W_f and W_g share a three-core and contain e together with the opposite displayed endpoints f,g.
      
      Write A for their common two-vertex part inside D and C=A union {e}. Then W_f=C union {f} and W_g=C union {g}. Apply the adjacent-four-window lemma fourwindows_force_a_pc2_square_or_a_twolabel_core_fan. If the five-set C union {f,g} is non-Hamiltonian, that lemma gives at least two Hamiltonian four-deletions with path-cover-two complements; at most one deletes e, so one deletion keeps e,f,g, producing the four-set Z in (3b). If the five-set is Hamiltonian, its complement is non-Hamiltonian with path-cover number two. Unless deleting one of the two vertices of A is already Hamiltonian (again producing such a Z), both of those deletions are non-Hamiltonian. Therefore no Hamilton path of the five-set can have an endpoint in A, because deleting a displayed endpoint of a Hamilton path leaves a Hamilton path. Hence both displayed endpoints lie in {e,f,g}, producing the five-set alternative of (3b).
      
      This combines the original bounded transport information with its endpoint-positioned consequence, so no sequential migration residue remains.

  • [reduces_to_no_trapping_of_deletiongenerated_threeside_states] The grand theorem reduces to no trapping of deletion-generated three-side states
      STATEMENT
      Let H be a minimum counterexample. For every exact deletion two-cover H-x=P|Q, with p=|P|>=q=|Q|, the trapped pairwise-repartition component containing the singleton lift P|Q|{x} also contains a spanning three-cover P^-|C|Q^+ whose component orders are {p-1,q-1,3}, where C is supported on x and the two facing endpoints of P,Q. The singleton lift reaches this state in two strict quadratic-potential descents. Consequently the grand two-cover conjecture follows from the order-independent statement that no deletion-generated three-side state of this form can lie in a trapped pairwise-repartition component. For |V(H)|>=14, every such state itself admits a further strict one-move quadratic descent.
      BODY / PROOF
      Assume H is a minimum counterexample and fix any exact deletion two-cover H-x=P|Q, with p=|P|>=q=|Q|. Its singleton lift S0=P|Q|{x} belongs to a trapped pairwise-repartition component, because any reachable cover with at most two components would two-cover H. By the certified theorem bc151d5d2a89, S0 reaches in two legal pairwise repartitions a state S2=P^-|C|Q^+ with |C|=3 and component-order multiset {p-1,q-1,3}; both moves strictly decrease Phi, by 2q-4 and 2p-6 respectively. Since reachability stays inside the same connected component, S2 is trapped as well. Therefore it is enough for grand-theorem closure to exclude trapped components containing these deletion-generated three-side states. No five-side branch is required: boundary antisymmetry chooses one of the two possible orders on the same three-vertex support C in all cases. Finally, when n=|V(H)|>=14, p>=ceil((n-1)/2)>=7, hence |P^-|>=6, and threesidedescent6 gives one additional strict legal descent from S2. Thus the theorem-facing no-trapping interface is a single three-side configuration, already equipped with a forced descending exit at large order.

    • [deletion_reachable_transport18] Above order seventeen deletion-generated descent reaches one of two synchronized transport residues
        STATEMENT
        Let H be a minimum counterexample of order n>=18 and let H-x=P|Q be any one-vertex deletion two-cover. The trapped pairwise-repartition component containing the singleton lift P|Q|{x} contains, after three strict quadratic-potential-decreasing moves, a spanning three-cover with a Hamiltonian side of order four or five. Moreover, within the same trapped component at least one of the following occurs: (1) a further legal pairwise repartition strictly decreases quadratic potential; (2) a reachable Hamiltonian four-side state carries the bounded path-cover-two transport package of four_window_transport15; (3) a reachable Hamiltonian five-side X has another component R=(r_1,...,r_m), m>=7, and some four-set C⊂V(X) such that both C∪{r_1} and C∪{r_m} are Hamiltonian.
        BODY / PROOF
        Start from the singleton lift S_0=P|Q|{x}. By bc151d5d2a89, two strict legal pairwise repartitions reach a deletion-generated three-side state S_2=X|R|T with |X|=3. Since n>=18, the larger inherited side in S_2 has order at least ceil((n-1)/2)-1>=8, so threesidedescent6 applies and gives a third strict legal repartition.
        
        Inspect the output of threesidedescent6. If one endpoint of the long side is absorbed into X, the new side has order four; call the resulting reachable state W|A|B. Apply four_window_transport15. Its first alternative is a further strict legal endpoint-transfer descent, giving (1). Otherwise its explicit bounded one/two-label path-cover-two transport package gives (2). All moves up to W|A|B, and any strict descent supplied there, lie in the same pairwise-repartition component as S_0.
        
        If instead both endpoint four-extensions of X are non-Hamiltonian, threesidedescent6 replaces X together with both ends of the long path by a Hamiltonian five-side Y and leaves the inherited interior of that long path. Thus the reachable state has component orders 5,p-3,q-1 up to relabelling, where p+q=n-1. The two non-five sides sum to n-5, so one has order at least ceil((n-5)/2)>=7 for n>=18. Call such a side R. Apply bc48e8bb931a to Y|R and the third component. Its endpoint-transfer alternative is a further strict legal repartition, again giving (1). Otherwise there is y∈V(Y) such that C=V(Y)-{y} extends Hamiltonianly with either displayed endpoint r_1,r_m of R, giving (3).
        
        Hence, after the universal deletion-generated descent segment, large-order trapping can only persist through one of two synchronized transport residues: an explicit pc2 square/extension package attached to a reachable four-side, or a common four-core on a reachable five-side extending to both ends of a long path. Bare order disagreement is not used.

      • [deletion_reachable_escape18] Large deletion states reach descent, pc2 transport, neutral support migration, or a positioned reversal
          STATEMENT
          Let H be a minimum counterexample of order n>=18 and let H-x=P|Q be any one-vertex deletion two-cover. In the trapped pairwise-repartition component containing the singleton lift, after the universal three strict quadratic-potential descents supplied by bc151d5d2a89 and threesidedescent6, at least one of the following occurs: (1) one further legal pairwise repartition strictly decreases quadratic potential; (2) a reachable Hamiltonian four-side state carries the bounded path-cover-two transport package of four_window_transport15; (3) a reachable Hamiltonian five-side state admits a one-move equal-Phi exchange of one five-side vertex with an endpoint of a long component; (4) in a reachable Hamiltonian five-side state, a five-side vertex participates in a tight triple reversing a displayed edge of a long component.
          BODY / PROOF
          By deletion_reachable_transport18, after three strict legal moves the component contains a reachable four-side or five-side state, and either a further strict descent already occurs, the four-side pc2 transport package occurs, or the five-side has a long component R of order at least seven together with a common four-core extending Hamiltonianly to both endpoints of R.
          
          In the first two cases we obtain (1) or (2). In the five-side case, apply five_side_arbitrary_escape01 directly to that reachable five-side and R. Its strict-descent outcome is (1). Its equal-size endpoint/support exchange is a legal pairwise repartition preserving Phi and gives (3). Its final outcome is a tight triple, using a vertex of the five-side, reversing a displayed edge of R, giving (4).
          
          Every cover mentioned before the pc2 transport package is reached by legal pairwise repartitions from the original deletion singleton lift, so the descent and neutral-exchange conclusions are genuinely component-respecting.

      • [deletion_reachable_overlap_transport18] Above order seventeen deletion-generated descent reaches endpoint overlap or a five-side common core
          STATEMENT
          Let H be a minimum counterexample of order n>=18 and let H-x=P|Q be any one-vertex deletion two-cover. In the pairwise-repartition component containing the singleton lift P|Q|{x}, three strict quadratic-potential-decreasing moves reach a spanning three-cover with a Hamiltonian side of order four or five. Moreover, within the same component at least one of the following occurs: (1) a further legal pairwise repartition strictly decreases quadratic potential; (2) a reachable Hamiltonian four-side W has another component R=(r_1,...,r_m), m>=7, and there are distinct a,b,c in W such that {r_1,r_m,a,b} and {r_1,r_m,a,c} are Hamiltonian four-sets with non-Hamiltonian path-cover-two complements; (3) a reachable Hamiltonian five-side Y has another component R=(r_1,...,r_m), m>=7, and some four-set C subset V(Y) such that both C union {r_1} and C union {r_m} are Hamiltonian. Thus the former generic reachable four-side transport package can be replaced by positioned endpoint-rooted overlap.
          BODY / PROOF
          Start from the singleton lift S0=P|Q|{x}. By bc151d5d2a89, two strict legal pairwise repartitions reach a deletion-generated three-side state S2=X|R|T with |X|=3. Since n>=18, the larger inherited side in S2 has order at least eight, so threesidedescent6 gives a third strict legal repartition. If this move absorbs one endpoint of the long side into X, the resulting reachable state has a Hamiltonian four-side W and the remainder of that long side still has order at least seven. Apply four_side_endpoint_overlap_descent_m6_01 to W and that long component. Its strict-descent outcome gives (1), while its other outcome gives two endpoint-rooted Hamiltonian four-sets sharing three vertices; their complements are non-Hamiltonian with path-cover number two, giving (2). If instead threesidedescent6 uses the double-endpoint branch, it produces a reachable Hamiltonian five-side Y. The other two components sum to n-5, so one has order at least seven. Apply bc48e8bb931a to Y and such a long component R. Its strict endpoint-transfer outcome gives (1); otherwise it gives a four-set C in Y extending Hamiltonianly with both displayed endpoints of R, giving (3). Every repartition used before outcomes (2) or (3), and every strict descent in (1), occurs inside the original pairwise-repartition component.

        • [deletion_reachable_transport16] From order sixteen every deletion state reaches strict descent, one neutral 5|6 transfer, or a synchronized small-side endpoint package
            STATEMENT
            Let H be a minimum counterexample of order n>=16 and let H-x=P|Q be any one-vertex deletion two-cover. From the singleton lift P|Q|{x}, three legal pairwise repartitions strictly decrease quadratic potential and reach a spanning three-cover with a Hamiltonian side of order four or five and another component of order at least six. Within the same pairwise-repartition component, at least one of the following then occurs: (1) a further legal repartition strictly decreases quadratic potential; (2) a reachable profile contains a five-side beside a six-path and admits the neutral endpoint transfer (5,6)->(6,5); (3) a reachable four-side X beside a path R=(r_1,...,r_m), m>=6, lies in the hard endpoint package: both X+{r_1}, X+{r_m} are non-Hamiltonian, for every t in X the five-set (X-{t}) union {r_1,r_m} is Hamiltonian and the inherited interior V(R)-{r_1,r_m} plus t is non-Hamiltonian with path-cover number two, and in particular two endpoint-rooted Hamiltonian four-sets sharing three vertices have a Hamiltonian five-vertex union; (4) a reachable five-side Y beside a path R of order at least six has a four-set C subset V(Y) such that C union {r_1} and C union {r_m} are Hamiltonian. For n>=18, outcome (2) is unnecessary: the relevant partner in the five-side branch has order at least seven, so the endpoint transfer is strict whenever it exists.
            BODY / PROOF
            Write the deletion cover sizes as p=|P|>=q=|Q|. By bc151d5d2a89, two strict legal moves from the singleton lift reach a state P^-|C|Q^+ with component orders p-1,3,q-1. Since n>=16, p>=ceil((n-1)/2)>=8, so |P^-|=p-1>=7. Apply threesidedescent6 to C|P^-. This is a third strict move. If the one-endpoint branch occurs, the new small side has order four and the remainder of P^- has order p-2>=6. Apply four_side_endpoint_package_m5_01 to that four-side and remainder. Any repartition produced there is strict because the partner has order at least six, yielding (1); otherwise its hard endpoint package gives (3), with pc2 residuals by minimum-counterexample calculus. If the two-endpoint branch of threesidedescent6 occurs, the new small side has order five and the other two component orders are p-3 and q-1. Their sum is n-5>=11. More sharply, max(p-3,q-1)>=6 for n>=16: if both were at most five then p<=8 and q<=6, so p+q<=14 and n<=15. Choose a partner R of order at least six and apply five_side_endpoint_core_m6_01. If its endpoint transfer occurs, it is neutral exactly when |R|=6, giving (2), and strict when |R|>=7, giving (1). Otherwise it gives the common four-core in (4). Finally, if n>=18 then max(p-3,q-1)>=7, since both at most six would imply p<=9,q<=7 and n=p+q+1<=17; hence the neutral equality case cannot arise in the five-side branch.

    • [reaches_a_fourwindow_descent_or_bounded_transport_state] Every deletion singleton component reaches a four-window descent or bounded transport state
        STATEMENT
        Let H be a minimum counterexample and let H-x=P|Q be any one-vertex deletion two-cover. In the pairwise-repartition component containing P|{x}|Q there is a three-cover W|R|S with W a Hamiltonian four-set and H-W=R|S a two-cover. Hence either |V(H)|<=14, or the component reaches a strict endpoint-transfer Phi descent from W|R|S, or it reaches the bounded path-cover-two transport package of four_window_transport_allorders01.
        BODY / PROOF
        By 8ededbb50716 the cyclic order from P|{x}|Q has a double-wrap rotation. The double-wrap theorem 687bbaa431c3 supplies a canonical tight four-path W whose complement has path-cover number two. By 5d81c7bd0407 the cyclic-interval three-covers arising from minimum cut sets form a connected subgraph of the pairwise-repartition graph, containing the original singleton lift and the double-wrap cover W|R|S. Apply four_window_transport_allorders01 to W and H-W=R|S. Its three alternatives give the stated small-order, strict-descent, and bounded-transport outcomes.

  • [compatibility_give_the_canonical_global_obstruction_interface] Defect-span three and deletion-cover compatibility give the canonical global obstruction interface
      STATEMENT
      A finite boundary tournament has a spanning cover by at most two tight paths exactly when some spanning ordering has defect span at most two. Every minimum counterexample has minimum defect span exactly three: any exact deletion cover P|Q of H-x yields the canonical ordering P,x,Q with defects confined to the three join centers and with the two outer centers always defective; if all three join triples are defective, the five-vertex join window reverses to a tight path. Deletion covers can be compared through compatibility: at least max(4,q+2) pairwise compatible q-path deletion covers glue to a global q-path cover. Pairwise support-compatible exact two-covers localize to one non-Hamiltonian class X with many Hamiltonian vertex deletions and one inert Hamiltonian class Q. For a compatible pair, the two omitted vertices must insert into the same common class at identical or adjacent slots; separated slots glue, while adjacent slots force a reversing triple through the unique intervening common vertex.
      BODY / PROOF
      # Defect-span three and deletion-cover compatibility give the canonical global obstruction interface
      
      Let H be a finite boundary tournament.
      
      ## Defect span and the exact two-cover reformulation
      
      For a spanning ordering
      pi=(v_1,...,v_n),
      call an internal position i a defect center when
      (v_{i-1},v_i,v_{i+1})
      is non-tight. If D(pi) is the set of defect centers, define span(pi)=0 when D(pi) is empty and otherwise
      span(pi)=max D(pi)-min D(pi)+1.
      
      Then H has a spanning cover by at most two tight paths if and only if some spanning ordering has defect span at most two.
      
      Indeed, concatenating two covering paths P=(v_1,...,v_j), Q=(v_{j+1},...,v_n) leaves possible defects only at the two join centers j,j+1. Conversely, if all defect centers lie in one such adjacent pair, the prefix through v_j and suffix from v_{j+1} are tight paths covering H.
      
      Now let H be a minimum counterexample and let
      H-x=P|Q
      be any exact deletion two-cover, with
      P=(p_0,...,p_m), Q=(q_0,...,q_s).
      The ordering
      (p_0,...,p_m,x,q_0,...,q_s)
      has defects only at the three centers p_m,x,q_0. The outer centers are necessarily defects: if (p_{m-1},p_m,x) were tight then (P,x)|Q would two-cover H; if (x,q_0,q_1) were tight then P|(x,Q) would. Therefore its defect span is exactly three. Since no counterexample admits span at most two, every minimum counterexample satisfies
      min_pi span(pi)=3.
      
      If the middle join triple (p_m,x,q_0) is also non-tight, boundary antisymmetry reverses all three failed join triples:
      (x,p_m,p_{m-1}), (q_0,x,p_m), (q_1,q_0,x)
      are tight. Hence
      (q_1,q_0,x,p_m,p_{m-1})
      is a tight five-vertex path.
      
      Thus closure is exactly defect compression from the canonical width-three window to width at most two.
      
      ## Compatible deletion covers glue globally
      
      An ordered path cover assigns to every ordered pair of vertices in its domain one of three pair states: same component with the first preceding the second, same component with the reverse precedence, or different components. Two covers are compatible on their intersection when all such pair states agree.
      
      Let q>=1 and D be a set of deletion labels with
      |D|>=max(4,q+2).
      For each d in D let F_d be a cover of H-d by at most q tight paths, and suppose every two F_d are compatible on their intersection.
      
      For distinct u,v choose d in D-{u,v}; compatibility makes the pair state independent of d. The induced same-component relation is transitive because any three vertices occur together in some F_d, except only the |D|=3 case which is excluded here. Each equivalence class inherits a total order, because every triple of vertices is seen inside one path cover. There are at most q classes, else q+1 representatives survive in some deletion cover. Every three consecutive vertices in a class remain consecutive in some F_d avoiding them, hence form a tight triple. Therefore the classes themselves are tight paths and give a global cover by at most q paths, restricting exactly to the deletion covers.
      
      For q=2, any four exact deletion covers in a counterexample cannot be mutually compatible.
      
      The threshold four is genuinely needed for exact one-path gluing. On four vertices {0,1,2,3}, take the tight triples
      (2,0,1),(1,0,3),(3,0,2),
      (0,1,2),(3,1,0),(2,1,3),
      (1,2,0),(0,2,3),(3,2,1),
      (0,3,1),(2,3,0),(1,3,2),
      with all reverses non-tight. The Hamilton paths
      (0,1,2), (0,2,3), (0,3,1)
      on the deletions of 3,1,2 are pairwise compatible, yet no Hamilton path on all four vertices exists. This does not contradict two-path coverability.
      
      ## Support-compatible families localize to one critical class
      
      Now assume pc(H)>2. Let |D|>=3 and let F_d be exact two-covers of H-d that are pairwise support-compatible: they agree only on whether common pairs lie in the same component, not necessarily on order.
      
      Define u~v using any F_d with d outside {u,v}. Support compatibility makes this well-defined. Transitivity follows by viewing triples inside one cover; in the only exceptional case D={u,v,w}, an auxiliary vertex outside D rules out a failure of transitivity using the two-component bound. Hence ~ is an equivalence relation with exactly two classes, say X,Q.
      
      All deletion labels lie in the same class. If a in D∩X and b in D∩Q, then F_b Hamiltonizes X and F_a Hamiltonizes Q, so X|Q would two-cover H. Thus D⊆X. Every F_d has support partition
      (X-{d}) | Q.
      Consequently H[Q] and every H[X-{d}] are Hamiltonian, while H[X] is non-Hamiltonian. One may normalize the Q-component to one fixed Hamilton order across the entire family. All remaining incompatibility is therefore relative-order disagreement inside the varying Hamilton paths on X-{d}.
      
      ## A compatible pair localizes to one insertion obstruction
      
      Take two exact deletion covers F_a of H-a and F_b of H-b that are fully compatible on
      W=V(H)-{a,b}.
      Their common pair data give exactly two nonempty ordered support classes P,Q. In F_a the missing vertex b is inserted at one slot of exactly one common class; in F_b the missing vertex a is inserted at one slot of one class.
      
      If a and b insert into different common classes, taking those two augmented components gives a spanning two-cover. Thus both insert into the same class, say
      P=(p_1,...,p_m),
      while Q is unchanged.
      
      If their insertion slots differ by at least two, insert both vertices into P at their respective slots. No consecutive triple contains both inserted vertices; every triple is inherited from one deletion cover or from the common P-order. The resulting path together with Q spans H, contradiction. Therefore compatible insertions use identical or adjacent slots.
      
      If the slots are adjacent, write the common order as
      P=L,z,R
      with
      F_b=(L,a,z,R)|Q,
      F_a=(L,z,b,R)|Q.
      Every triple of
      (L,a,z,b,R)
      is certified except possibly (a,z,b). If that triple were tight, the displayed path with Q would two-cover H. Hence (a,z,b) is non-tight, and boundary antisymmetry forces
      (b,z,a)
      tight.
      
      Thus deletion compatibility supplies the exact local obstruction interface for defect compression: four compatible states glue globally; a support-compatible family collapses to one critical Hamilton-deletion class; and a compatible pair can fail only through a single common insertion slot or an adjacent-slot reversing triple.

    • [centralbridge35] Every deletion state has a canonical bounded central-bridge three-cover
        STATEMENT
        Let H be a minimum counterexample and H-x=P|Q an exact deletion two-cover with P=(p0,...,pm), Q=(q0,...,qs). Then H has a spanning three-path cover whose central component is supported on the join window and has order either three or five: if (pm,x,q0) is tight, use (p0,...,p_{m-1}) | (pm,x,q0) | (q1,...,qs); if it is non-tight, use (p0,...,p_{m-2}) | (q1,q0,x,pm,p_{m-1}) | (q2,...,qs).
        BODY / PROOF
        Let (H) be a minimum counterexample and let
        [
        H-x=P|Q
        ]
        be an exact two-path cover, where
        [
        P=(p_0,ldots,p_m),qquad Q=(q_0,ldots,q_s).
        ]
        Every component of a one-vertex deletion cover in a minimum counterexample has order at least three, so (m,sge2).
        
        The two outer join triples are non-tight:
        [
        (p_{m-1},p_m,x)quad	ext{and}quad(x,q_0,q_1).
        ]
        Otherwise (x) could be appended to (P) or prepended to (Q), giving a spanning two-cover.
        
        By boundary antisymmetry their reversal mates are tight:
        [
        (x,p_m,p_{m-1})
        quad	ext{and}quad
        (q_1,q_0,x).
        ]
        
        Now distinguish the middle join triple.
        
        ### Case 1: ((p_m,x,q_0)) is tight
        
        Then
        [
        C=(p_m,x,q_0)
        ]
        is a tight three-path. The inherited contiguous subpaths
        [
        P^-=(p_0,ldots,p_{m-1}),
        qquad
        Q^+=(q_1,ldots,q_s)
        ]
        are tight, pairwise disjoint from (C), and their supports partition (V(H)).
        
        Hence
        [
        P^-|C|Q^+
        ]
        is a spanning three-path cover with central component of order three.
        
        ### Case 2: ((p_m,x,q_0)) is non-tight
        
        Boundary antisymmetry gives
        [
        (q_0,x,p_m)
        ]
        tight. Together with the two already forced reversed outer joins,
        [
        (q_1,q_0,x),qquad (x,p_m,p_{m-1}),
        ]
        this makes
        [
        C=(q_1,q_0,x,p_m,p_{m-1})
        ]
        a tight five-path.
        
        The inherited contiguous subpaths
        [
        P^{--}=(p_0,ldots,p_{m-2}),
        qquad
        Q^{++}=(q_2,ldots,q_s)
        ]
        are tight and nonempty, and together with (C) partition (V(H)).
        
        Hence
        [
        P^{--}|C|Q^{++}
        ]
        is a spanning three-path cover with central component of order five.
        
        Therefore every exact deletion state admits a canonical spanning three-cover obtained by replacing its width-three defect window by one bounded tight bridge component of order (3) or (5). No reversal of a tight path is used.

      • [centralbridgereach] Every deletion state reaches its canonical central bridge in two Astra moves
          STATEMENT
          Let H be a minimum counterexample and H-x=P|Q an exact deletion two-cover, with P=(p0,...,pm), Q=(q0,...,qs). Regard P|Q|(x) as a spanning three-cover. The canonical bridge state of centralbridge35 lies in the same Astra-003 component and is reached in exactly two explicit pairwise repartitions. If (pm,x,q0) is tight, first repartition Q|(x) as (x,q0)|Q+ and then repartition P|(x,q0) as P-|(pm,x,q0). If (pm,x,q0) is non-tight, first repartition Q|(x) as (q1,q0,x)|Q++ and then repartition P|(q1,q0,x) as P--|(q1,q0,x,pm,p_{m-1}). In particular the 5-bridge route passes through a spanning three-cover with a three-vertex component after one move.
          BODY / PROOF
          Let
          
          H-x=P|Q
          
          be an exact deletion two-cover in a minimum counterexample, with
          
          P=(p_0,...,p_m),
          Q=(q_0,...,q_s).
          
          By the minimum-counterexample deletion-cover bound, both components have order at least three, so all tails used below are nonempty.
          
          Start from the spanning three-cover
          
          P | Q | (x).
          
          The two outer join triples
          
          (p_{m-1},p_m,x)
          and
          (x,q_0,q_1)
          
          are non-tight, since either would absorb x into one deletion-cover component and give a spanning two-cover with the other component. Hence
          
          (x,p_m,p_{m-1})
          and
          (q_1,q_0,x)
          
          are tight by boundary antisymmetry.
          
          We treat the middle join.
          
          ## Case 1: (p_m,x,q_0) is tight
          
          First repartition the pair Q|(x). Its union has the exact two-cover
          
          (x,q_0) | Q^+,
          
          where
          
          Q^+=(q_1,...,q_s).
          
          The two-vertex component is automatically a tight path, and Q^+ is an inherited contiguous subpath. Thus
          
          P | (x,q_0) | Q^+
          
          is reached by one legal Astra move.
          
          Now repartition P|(x,q_0). Their union has the exact two-cover
          
          P^- | C,
          
          where
          
          P^-=(p_0,...,p_{m-1})
          and
          C=(p_m,x,q_0).
          
          The path P^- is inherited and C is tight by the case assumption. Hence the second legal move reaches
          
          P^- | (p_m,x,q_0) | Q^+,
          
          which is exactly the order-three canonical bridge state of centralbridge35.
          
          ## Case 2: (p_m,x,q_0) is non-tight
          
          Boundary antisymmetry gives
          
          (q_0,x,p_m)
          
          tight.
          
          First repartition Q|(x). Since the already forced triple
          
          (q_1,q_0,x)
          
          is tight, their union has the exact two-cover
          
          T_Q | Q^{++},
          
          where
          
          T_Q=(q_1,q_0,x)
          and
          Q^{++}=(q_2,...,q_s).
          
          Thus one legal move gives
          
          P | T_Q | Q^{++}.
          
          In particular, already after one move the component contains a spanning three-cover with a three-vertex component.
          
          Now repartition P|T_Q. Their union has the exact two-cover
          
          P^{--} | C,
          
          where
          
          P^{--}=(p_0,...,p_{m-2})
          
          and
          
          C=(q_1,q_0,x,p_m,p_{m-1}).
          
          The path P^{--} is inherited. The three consecutive triples of C are
          
          (q_1,q_0,x),
          (q_0,x,p_m),
          (x,p_m,p_{m-1}),
          
          all of which are tight by the forced outer reversals and the middle-case reversal. Hence C is a tight five-path.
          
          The second legal move therefore reaches
          
          P^{--} | (q_1,q_0,x,p_m,p_{m-1}) | Q^{++},
          
          the canonical order-five bridge state of centralbridge35.
          
          Thus in both middle orientations the canonical bridge is not merely an existential spanning cover: it lies within Astra distance two of the original deletion state.
          
          Equivalently, every exact deletion state and its canonical bounded cross-component bridge belong to the same Astra connected component. Moreover the five-bridge branch factors through an explicit order-three state after its first move.

        • [threesidedescent6] Every three-side next to a path of order at least six has a strict one-move quadratic descent
            STATEMENT
            Let C=X|P|Q be any spanning three-path cover of a boundary tournament, where X is a tight path of order three and P=(p_1,...,p_m) has m>=6. Then one legal pairwise repartition of X|P produces another spanning three-path cover C_prime with strictly smaller quadratic potential. More precisely, either X union {p_1} or X union {p_m} is Hamiltonian, yielding component orders 4 and m-1 and potential drop 2m-8; or both four-sets are non-Hamiltonian, in which case X union {p_1,p_m} is Hamiltonian by localextend01 and yields component orders 5 and m-2 with potential drop 4m-20.
            BODY / PROOF
            Let
            
            C = X | P | Q
            
            be a spanning three-path cover, where |X|=3 and
            
            P=(p_1,...,p_m)
            
            has m>=6. Write
            
            Phi(C)=sum_i |P_i|^2.
            
            We inspect the two endpoint extensions
            
            X union {p_1},
            X union {p_m}.
            
            If at least one is Hamiltonian, say X union {p_1}, repartition the pair X|P as
            
            (X union {p_1}) | (p_2,...,p_m).
            
            Both displayed parts are tight paths: the first by hypothesis, the second as an inherited contiguous subpath of P. The old contribution of X|P to Phi is
            
            3^2 + m^2,
            
            while the new contribution is
            
            4^2 + (m-1)^2.
            
            Hence
            
            Phi(C)-Phi(C')
            = 9+m^2 - [16+(m-1)^2]
            = 2m-8 > 0.
            
            The same argument applies if X union {p_m} is Hamiltonian.
            
            It remains to suppose that both endpoint four-sets
            
            X union {p_1}
            and
            X union {p_m}
            
            are non-Hamiltonian.
            
            Apply the certified local-extension lemma from localextend01, “Two bad four-extensions force a controlled five-path,” to the fixed tight three-path X and the exterior vertices p_1,p_m. It gives a Hamilton tight path on
            
            X union {p_1,p_m}.
            
            Therefore X|P can be repartitioned as
            
            (X union {p_1,p_m}) | (p_2,...,p_{m-1}).
            
            The second part is again an inherited contiguous path and is nonempty because m>=6.
            
            The old Phi contribution is again
            
            9+m^2,
            
            whereas the new contribution is
            
            5^2+(m-2)^2.
            
            Thus
            
            Phi(C)-Phi(C')
            =9+m^2-[25+(m-2)^2]
            =4m-20 >0
            
            for m>=6.
            
            Hence in every case a single legal repartition move strictly decreases Phi.
            
            No trappedness or Phi-minimality assumption is used. The theorem is an arbitrary-state descent rule.
            
            Consequently, whenever the canonical central-bridge construction produces a three-vertex path component, that component can coexist with a path component of order at least six only transiently: the state has an immediate strict quadratic descent involving those two path components.

          • [beside_a_path_of_order_at_least_six_admit_a_twomove_descent] Two four-vertex paths beside a path of order at least six admit a two-move descent
              STATEMENT
              Let A|B|P be any spanning three-cover of a boundary tournament with |A|=|B|=4 and |P|=m>=6. Two legal pairwise repartitions reach a three-cover of strictly smaller quadratic potential. The decrease is at least min(2m-10,4m-22)>=2. Consequently this size profile cannot minimize Phi in its pairwise-repartition component.
              BODY / PROOF
              Choose distinct vertices u,v of A and a displayed Hamilton order (b_0,b_1,b_2,b_3) on B. If either B union {u} or B union {v} is Hamiltonian, choose that Hamiltonian five-set S. Otherwise apply repeated bad deletion in localextend01 to B,u,v: the set {b_0,b_1,b_2,u,v} is Hamiltonian, and choose it as S. Thus in all cases A union B contains a Hamiltonian five-set S.
              
              Its complement T within A union B has three vertices, and every three-vertex boundary tournament admits a Hamilton path by reversal antisymmetry. Repartition A|B into S|T, leaving P unchanged. The potential increases by 5^2+3^2-4^2-4^2=2.
              
              Now apply threesidedescent6 to T|P with S fixed. This second legal move decreases the potential by either 2m-8 or 4m-20. Relative to the original cover, the total decrease is therefore either 2m-10 or 4m-22, each strictly positive for m>=6. The two possible final order profiles are 5,4,m-1 and 5,5,m-2. Both moves stay within the same pairwise-repartition component. No restriction on m beyond the stated inequality and no order enumeration is used.

          • [bound_excludes_short_sides_from_every_twocover_of_a_pairunion] A product bound excludes short sides from every two-cover of a pair-union
              STATEMENT
              Let F=A|B|P minimize Phi in a connected component of the pairwise-repartition graph containing no cover with at most two paths. Put a=|A|>=3, b=|B|>=3, and c=|P|>=6. If c>(a-3)(b-3)+4, then every two-cover of H[V(A) union V(B)] has both path orders at least four. In particular that union has no Hamiltonian support of order at least a+b-3.
              BODY / PROOF
              Write s=a+b and W=V(A) union V(B). Trappedness excludes a Hamilton path on W, since it could replace A|B and give a spanning two-cover together with P.
              
              Suppose W has a two-cover U|V with |U|<=3. If |U|=3 it already has orders 3,s-3.
