Thus endpoint Hamiltonicity of the first complementary label transports along C until it produces an explicit reversible component-end edge.
                      BODY / PROOF
                      Start with the assumed Hamilton path R_0 ending at c_0. Inductively, if R_h=(...,q,c_h) is a Hamilton path on X union {c_0,...,c_h} and (q,c_h,c_{h+1}) is tight, append c_{h+1} to obtain R_{h+1}. If this succeeds for every h<m, then R_m is a Hamilton path on X union V(C); together with the disjoint tight path D it gives a spanning two-cover of H, contrary to pc(H)>2. Hence there is a first h<m for which (q,c_h,c_{h+1}) is non-tight. Boundary antisymmetry gives the tight reverse (c_{h+1},c_h,q), which reverses the terminal ordered edge (q,c_h) of R_h. Every intermediate state R_h | C[h+1,m] | D is a spanning three-cover, so the reversal is already located at a genuine component end. The proof for a Hamilton order beginning at c_0 follows by reversing the direction of the greedy transport along C.

                    • [endpoint_hamiltonicity_transport_or_crossing01] Endpoint Hamiltonicity yields either greedy end-hook transport or a forced coarse support crossing
                        STATEMENT
                        Let H be a minimum counterexample and let X|C|D be a spanning three-cover, where H[X] is Hamiltonian, C=(c_0,c_1,...,c_m) is a nontrivial tight path with m>=1, and D is a nonempty tight path. Suppose H[X union {c_0}] is Hamiltonian. Then at least one of the following holds. (1) Some Hamilton tight path on X union {c_0} has c_0 as an endpoint; in that case the greedy endpoint-transport theorem 883bd2af7e73 applies and, after absorbing a maximal initial segment c_0,...,c_h of C into X, produces an explicit tight triple reversing the terminal or initial edge of the enlarged Hamilton component. (2) The vertex c_0 is internal in every Hamilton tight path on X union {c_0}; in that case every two-cover of H-c_0 contains an ordinary edge crossing the coarse bipartition X | ((V(C)-{c_0}) union V(D)), and by 5ff05be1a5bc every such deletion cover has at least two crossings of the finer four-class partition obtained by deleting c_0 from a Hamilton path on X+c_0. Thus endpoint Hamiltonicity never remains a structureless local fact: it yields either a reversible component-end edge after finite monotone transport along C, or unavoidable support mixing across the original three-cover cut.
                        BODY / PROOF
                        Choose any Hamilton path R on X union {c_0}. If there exists a Hamilton order with c_0 at one end, apply 883bd2af7e73 in the matching orientation. It greedily appends consecutive vertices of C until the first failed append; boundary antisymmetry then gives a tight triple reversing the current component-end edge. This is outcome (1). If no Hamilton order places c_0 at an end, then c_0 is permanently internal. Apply permanent_internal_coarse_crossing01 to obtain the forced crossing of the coarse cut X | ((C-c_0) union D) in every deletion two-cover of H-c_0. Apply 5ff05be1a5bc to the same Hamilton enlargement to obtain the simultaneous lower bound of two crossings across the finer four-piece split. This is outcome (2). The two cases exhaust Hamilton orders on X+c_0.

                  • [adjacent_barrier_families_force_three_cyclic_mixed_fourpaths] Adjacent barrier families force three cyclic mixed four-paths
                      STATEMENT
                      Assume case (3), the synchronized endpoint-barrier branch, of e5d3ccfef9bb. Then for every i modulo three the ordered four-tuple (b_i,t_i,t_{i+2},a_{i+1}) is a tight path. Hence the barrier residue contains the cyclic family Q_i=(b_i,t_i,t_{i+2},a_{i+1}), i=1,2,3, whose pairwise overlaps are exactly transferred labels.
                      BODY / PROOF
                      Fix i. Since t_{i+2} is the initial endpoint of A_{i+2}, it belongs to E_i. The initial barrier family from e5d3ccfef9bb therefore gives (b_i,t_i,t_{i+2}) tight. Next, t_i is the initial endpoint of A_i, hence t_i belongs to E_{i+1}. The terminal barrier family for support S_{i+1} gives (t_i,t_{i+2},a_{i+1}) tight. These are exactly the two consecutive triples of the ordered four-tuple (b_i,t_i,t_{i+2},a_{i+1}), so it is a tight path. No rotation or reversal of an ordered tight triple is used. Apply cyclically.

                    • [barrier_branch_already_forces_standard_order_disagreement] The synchronized barrier branch already forces standard order disagreement
                        STATEMENT
                        Assume the synchronized endpoint-barrier branch of the all-equal {1,1,1} support triangle. Then explicit relative-order disagreement is forced between tight paths. Indeed, for every i the mixed tight four-path Q_i=(b_i,t_i,t_{i+2},a_{i+1}) orders the common vertices b_i,t_i oppositely to the displayed support path P_i=(t_i,b_i,...,a_i,t_{i+1}). Consequently the path-intersection calculus yields a reversed common ordered edge, a tight triple reversing an ordered edge at an intersection, or a vertex-simple tight cycle.
                        BODY / PROOF
                        By 2bac72daae4a, Q_i=(b_i,t_i,t_{i+2},a_{i+1}) is a tight path. The displayed Hamilton path P_i on S_i begins (t_i,b_i). Thus P_i and Q_i have common vertices t_i,b_i, occurring in opposite relative orders. Apply Section 4 of pathcalc01, which is explicitly valid for arbitrary tight paths with differing supports. It yields one of the standard local order-disturbance witnesses: a reversed common ordered edge, a reversing tight triple at an intersection, or a vertex-simple tight cycle. No cyclic rotation of ordered triples is used.

                    • [branch_canonically_enters_the_fourside_complement_frontier] The all-equal barrier branch canonically enters the four-side complement frontier
                        STATEMENT
                        Assume the synchronized endpoint-barrier branch of e5d3ccfef9bb. For each i modulo three let Q_i=(b_i,t_i,t_{i+2},a_{i+1}), the certified tight four-path from 2bac72daae4a. Then V(Q_i) is a Hamiltonian four-vertex support and H-V(Q_i) is non-Hamiltonian with path-cover number two. Hence choosing any two-cover P_i|R_i of H-V(Q_i) gives a spanning three-cover Q_i|P_i|R_i with a four-vertex path. The three four-sides are cyclically linked: Q_i and Q_{i+1} intersect exactly in t_i, and their union pattern is fixed by the transferred labels.
                        BODY / PROOF
                        By 2bac72daae4a each Q_i is a tight four-vertex path, so its support is Hamiltonian. It is proper because the all-equal minimum counterexample has order n=3r>10. Minimum-counterexample calculus therefore gives pc(H-V(Q_i))<=2. The complement cannot be Hamiltonian: otherwise a Hamilton path on H-V(Q_i) together with Q_i would be a spanning two-cover of H. Thus pc(H-V(Q_i))=2. Choosing any two-cover P_i|R_i of the complement yields the stated three-cover. Pairwise overlap follows directly from Q_i={b_i,t_i,t_{i+2},a_{i+1}} and Q_{i+1}={b_{i+1},t_{i+1},t_i,a_{i+2}}; in the all-equal minimum-counterexample setting the endpoint labels are distinct, so the intersection is exactly {t_i}.

                  • [barriers_force_reverse_hooks_on_the_first_internal_edges] Synchronized endpoint barriers force reverse hooks on the first internal edges
                      STATEMENT
                      Assume the endpoint-barrier branch of e5d3ccfef9bb and |M_i|>=2. Write M_i=(b_i,c_i,...,z_i,a_i), where c_i is the second vertex and z_i the penultimate vertex of M_i (so for |M_i|=2, c_i=a_i and z_i=b_i). Then for every complementary endpoint d in E_i, both (c_i,b_i,d) and (d,a_i,z_i) are tight. Thus every blocked complementary endpoint creates reverse hooks on both first internal edges of the displayed support path P_i, uniformly in the length of M_i.
                      BODY / PROOF
                      Fix d in E_i in the endpoint-barrier branch. By definition of this branch, H[S_i union {d}] is non-Hamiltonian, so d is automatically noninsertable into the displayed Hamilton path P_i=(t_i,b_i,c_i,...,z_i,a_i,t_{i+1}). The start barrier from e5d3ccfef9bb is (b_i,t_i,d), hence by cyclic invariance also (t_i,d,b_i) is tight. If (d,b_i,c_i) were tight, inserting d immediately after t_i in P_i would give a Hamilton path on S_i union {d}, contradiction. Hence (d,b_i,c_i) is non-tight, and boundary antisymmetry gives (c_i,b_i,d) tight. Dually, the terminal barrier (d,t_{i+1},a_i) cyclically gives (a_i,d,t_{i+1}) tight. If (z_i,a_i,d) were tight, inserting d immediately before t_{i+1} would Hamiltonize S_i union {d}, again a contradiction. Therefore its reverse (d,a_i,z_i) is tight. Apply to every d and every i.

                  • [endpoint_forces_double_crossing_in_every_deletion_cover] A permanently internal complementary endpoint forces double crossing in every deletion cover
                      STATEMENT
                      Let H be a minimum counterexample and let X|C|D be a spanning three-cover, where X is Hamiltonian, C=(c_0,c_1,...,c_m) and D are nonempty tight paths, and m>=1. Suppose H[X union {c_0}] is Hamiltonian but c_0 is internal in every Hamilton tight path on X union {c_0}. Then for any Hamilton path R on X union {c_0}, deleting c_0 splits R into two nonempty tight paths L|R^+, and every two-cover T of H-c_0 has at least two ordinary edges crossing the four-class partition V(L)|V(R^+)|V(C-c_0)|V(D).
                      BODY / PROOF
                      Choose a Hamilton path R on X union {c_0}. Permanent internality means c_0 is not an endpoint of R, so deleting c_0 leaves two nonempty contiguous tight subpaths L and R^+. Since m>=1, C-c_0 is a nonempty tight path, and D is nonempty by hypothesis. Hence H-c_0 has a displayed four-path cover L|R^+|(C-c_0)|D, and each of the four partition classes is Hamiltonian. Let T be any two-cover of H-c_0, which exists by minimum-counterexample calculus. Apply the transition-count identity of coversurg01 Section 6 to the four-class partition and q=2. Since each class has path-cover number one, the number t of ordinary T-edges joining distinct classes satisfies t >= 1+1+1+1-2 = 2. Thus every deletion cover of H-c_0 has at least two support crossings relative to the canonical four-piece split created by the permanently internal vertex.

                    • [permanent_internal_coarse_crossing01] A permanently internal absorbed endpoint forces a crossing of the original support cut
                        STATEMENT
                        Let H be a minimum counterexample and let X|C|D be a spanning three-cover, where H[X] is Hamiltonian, C=(c_0,c_1,...,c_m) is a nontrivial tight path with m>=1, and D is a nonempty tight path. Suppose H[X union {c_0}] is Hamiltonian and c_0 is internal in every Hamilton tight path on X union {c_0}. Then every exact two-cover T of H-c_0 contains an ordinary path edge with one endpoint in X and the other endpoint in (V(C)-{c_0}) union V(D). Equivalently, no deletion two-cover of H-c_0 respects the coarse bipartition X | ((C-c_0) union D). Combined with 5ff05be1a5bc, every such T has at least two crossings of the finer four-class split induced by deleting c_0 from a Hamilton path on X+c_0, and at least one of those crossings necessarily crosses this coarse original-support cut.
                        BODY / PROOF
                        Fix any Hamilton path R on X union {c_0}; by hypothesis c_0 is internal in R, though only Hamiltonicity of X+c_0 is needed for the coarse-cut conclusion. Put B=(V(C)-{c_0}) union V(D), so V(H-c_0)=X disjoint-union B and both sides are nonempty. Let T=T_1|T_2 be any exact two-cover of H-c_0. Suppose for contradiction that no ordinary edge of either T-component crosses the cut X|B. Then every T-component is contained entirely in one side of the cut: along a path, moving from a vertex of X to a vertex of B would itself use a crossing ordinary edge. Since T covers both nonempty sides and has exactly two components, after relabelling T_1 is a Hamilton path on X and T_2 is a Hamilton path on B. But H[X union {c_0}] is Hamiltonian by hypothesis, so choose any Hamilton path R_0 on X union {c_0}. Then R_0 | T_2 is a spanning two-cover of H, contradicting that H is a minimum counterexample and hence has path-cover number greater than two. Therefore every exact two-cover of H-c_0 has at least one X-B crossing edge. The final sentence follows by combining this conclusion with the certified finer four-class crossing theorem 5ff05be1a5bc.

                    • [permanentinternal_covers_have_only_three_contracted_block_forms] Equality-two-crossing permanent-internal covers have only three contracted block forms
                        STATEMENT
                        Continue the setting of 5ff05be1a5bc. Let T be a two-cover of H-c_0 having exactly two crossing edges across the four classes L, R^+, C^*=C-c_0, D. Then each class occurs as one intact T-block. After contracting the four blocks, the two T-components have exactly one of three possible support forms: (I) L-C^* and R^+-D; (II) L-D and R^+-C^*; or (III) one three-block path using L,R^+,C^* in some order while D is the other isolated component. In particular, C^*, L, and R^+ can never be isolated components, and the matching L-R^+ together with C^*-D is impossible.
                        BODY / PROOF
                        Because T has q=2 and exactly two cross-class edges, equality holds in coversurg01 Section 6 for the four-class partition from 5ff05be1a5bc. Hence each class contributes exactly one nonempty block. Contracting the four blocks turns T into a two-edge path forest on four vertices, so its abstract form is either 2K2 or P3 plus an isolated vertex. If C^* is isolated, replace that component by the inherited tight path C=(c_0,C^*) and leave the other T-component unchanged, giving a spanning two-cover of H. If L is isolated, append c_0 using the inherited prefix (L,c_0) of the Hamilton path (L,c_0,R^+); similarly if R^+ is isolated, prepend c_0 using (c_0,R^+). Each again gives a spanning two-cover. Thus in the P3+isolated case only D may be isolated, forcing form III. In the 2K2 case, if L is paired with R^+, then the other pair is C^* with D; replace the L-R^+ component by the known Hamilton path (L,c_0,R^+) and retain the C^*-D component, again two-covering H. Therefore the L-R^+ matching is impossible. The only remaining perfect matchings are forms I and II.

                  • [force_mixed_hamiltonian_fivesets_with_twocoverable_complements] Three endpoint barriers force mixed Hamiltonian five-sets with two-coverable complements
                      STATEMENT
                      Assume the endpoint-barrier branch of e5d3ccfef9bb. Fix i and choose any three distinct vertices d_1,d_2,d_3 in E_i. Then both five-sets {t_i,b_i,d_1,d_2,d_3} and {a_i,t_{i+1},d_1,d_2,d_3} are Hamiltonian. Since H is a minimum counterexample, the complement of each proper Hamiltonian five-set is non-Hamiltonian and has path-cover number two. Thus whenever |E_i|>=3, the all-equal residue supplies, at each end of S_i, a family of bounded mixed Hamiltonian supports with two-coverable non-Hamiltonian complements.
                      BODY / PROOF
                      For each d in E_i, e5d3ccfef9bb gives (b_i,t_i,d) tight, hence by cyclic invariance (t_i,d,b_i) tight. Apply the certified three-common-endpoint Hamilton-five-path lemma in smallset01 with outer vertices t_i,b_i and middle vertices d_1,d_2,d_3. This gives a Hamilton path on {t_i,b_i,d_1,d_2,d_3}. Likewise the terminal barriers (d,t_{i+1},a_i) cyclically give (a_i,d,t_{i+1}) for all d, so the same lemma gives Hamiltonicity of {a_i,t_{i+1},d_1,d_2,d_3}. Each five-set is proper. By the minimum-counterexample calculus, the complement of any proper Hamiltonian support has path-cover number two; it cannot be Hamiltonian, since otherwise H itself would have a spanning two-cover.

                    • [endpoints_force_a_hamiltonian_sixset_or_order_disagreement] Four complementary endpoints force a Hamiltonian six-set or order disagreement
                        STATEMENT
                        Assume the endpoint-barrier branch of the all-equal {1,1,1} support triangle in a minimum counterexample. Then for every i the complementary endpoint set E_i has four distinct vertices. Put K_i={t_i,b_i} union E_i. Either H[K_i] is Hamiltonian, in which case its proper complement is non-Hamiltonian with path-cover number two, or H[K_i] is non-Hamiltonian and the four Hamiltonian five-vertex deletions K_i-d, d in E_i, force relative-order disagreement: for arbitrary Hamilton paths chosen on those four deletions, some two order a common pair differently. The analogous statement holds at the terminal end with {a_i,t_{i+1}} in place of {t_i,b_i}.
                        BODY / PROOF
                        By the certified supported four-of-six theorem in smallset01, every six-vertex boundary tournament has a Hamiltonian five-vertex induced subtournament; adjoining the remaining singleton gives a spanning two-cover. A three-vertex boundary tournament is itself Hamiltonian by boundary antisymmetry. Hence a minimum counterexample cannot have order 3 or 6. In the all-equal cube |V(H)|=3r, so r>=3. Therefore each M_j has order r-1>=2 and each A_j has order r>=3; consequently the complementary two-cover M_{i+1}|A_{i+2} has four distinct displayed endpoints, so |E_i|=4. By b7ac977975b4, for every d in E_i the five-set K_i-d={t_i,b_i} union (E_i-{d}) is Hamiltonian. If K_i is non-Hamiltonian, apply astra004fourgooddisagree with D=E_i to H[K_i], yielding relative-order disagreement for arbitrary Hamilton paths on the four deletions. If K_i is Hamiltonian, minimum-counterexample calculus gives a two-cover of the proper complement; that complement cannot be Hamiltonian, since together with K_i it would give a spanning two-cover of H. The terminal-end statement is identical using the second family of Hamiltonian five-sets from b7ac977975b4.

                      • [barrier_residue_is_a_synchronized_sixsupport_family] The order-neutral barrier residue is a synchronized six-support family
                          STATEMENT
                          In the endpoint-barrier branch of the all-equal {1,1,1} support triangle, either a relative-order disagreement is already forced by one of the six endpoint tests, or for every i both six-sets L_i={t_i,b_i} union E_i and R_i={a_i,t_{i+1}} union E_i are Hamiltonian. In the latter branch each complement H-L_i and H-R_i is non-Hamiltonian with path-cover number two. Thus after excluding standard order disturbance, the all-equal barrier residue reduces to six synchronized Hamiltonian supports, two over the same four-endpoint set E_i at each of the three cyclic positions.
                          BODY / PROOF
                          For each i, 996c0ca32fbb applies to the initial-end pair {t_i,b_i} and, symmetrically, to the terminal-end pair {a_i,t_{i+1}}. If any of the resulting six induced six-vertex tournaments is non-Hamiltonian, the corresponding four Hamiltonian endpoint deletions force relative-order disagreement. If no such disagreement occurs, all six induced six-vertex tournaments must therefore be Hamiltonian. Minimum-counterexample calculus then gives a two-cover of each proper complement, and each such complement is non-Hamiltonian because a Hamiltonian complement together with the six-support would two-cover H.

                  • [support_triangle_always_forces_relativeorder_disagreement] The all-equal support triangle always forces relative-order disagreement
                      STATEMENT
                      In the all-equal {1,1,1} support-triangle setting, relative-order disagreement between tight paths is unavoidable. More precisely, the displayed support paths P_i=(t_i,M_i,t_{i+1}) together with endpoint insertion/barrier alternatives force two tight paths that order a common vertex pair differently. Hence the path-intersection calculus yields a reversed common ordered edge, a reversing tight triple at an intersection, or a vertex-simple tight cycle.
                      BODY / PROOF
                      For each i modulo three, consider the special complementary endpoint x_i=t_{i+2}, which lies in E_i because it is the initial endpoint of A_{i+2}. If x_i is noninsertable into the displayed order P_i and H[S_i union {x_i}] is Hamiltonian, noninsertableorderdisagree01 gives relative-order disagreement immediately. If x_i is noninsertable and H[S_i union {x_i}] is non-Hamiltonian, apply the terminal-end barrier proposition from coversurg01 to S_i with D={x_i}. This gives the tight triple (t_{i+2},t_{i+1},a_i). But P_{i+1}=(t_{i+1},M_{i+1},t_{i+2}) orders the common vertices t_{i+1},t_{i+2} in the opposite order, so Section 4 of pathcalc01 gives relative-order disagreement. Therefore, if no relative-order disagreement occurs anywhere, every x_i=t_{i+2} must be insertable into P_i. Let R_i be the resulting tight Hamilton path on S_i union {t_{i+2}}, obtained by inserting t_{i+2} into the displayed order P_i. All three R_i contain the transferred-label triple T={t_1,t_2,t_3}. Deleting the inserted label from R_i leaves P_i, so R_i preserves the relation t_i before t_{i+1}. Thus R_1 forces t_1<t_2 on T, R_2 forces t_2<t_3, and R_3 forces t_3<t_1. If the three R_i induced one common relative order on T these inequalities would form a cyclic strict order, impossible. Hence some pair R_i,R_j orders two common transferred labels differently. Applying pathcalc01 again gives standard relative-order disagreement. Thus every branch forces order disturbance.

                    • [insertion_forces_a_cyclic_support_or_an_explicit_endpoint_hook] A failed transferred-label insertion forces a cyclic support or an explicit endpoint hook
                        STATEMENT
                        In the all-equal support-triangle setting, fix j modulo three and suppose the transferred label t_{j+1} is noninsertable into P_{j-1}, with H[S_{j-1} union {t_{j+1}}] non-Hamiltonian. Then, writing P_j=(t_j,b_j,...,a_j,t_{j+1}), at least one of the following holds: (1) (t_j,t_{j+1},a_j) is tight; (2) (b_j,t_j,t_{j+1}) is tight; or (3) S_j has the tight cyclic order (t_{j+1},t_j,b_j,...,a_j). Thus the noninsertable/non-Hamiltonian branch of the all-equal argument yields an explicit endpoint hook at one end of the adjacent support or makes that entire support cyclic.
                        BODY / PROOF
                        The terminal barrier for S_{j-1}, applied to d=t_{j+1}, gives Q=(t_{j+1},t_j,a_{j-1}) as a tight path. Compare Q with P_j=(t_j,b_j,...,a_j,t_{j+1}). Their only common vertices are the endpoints t_j,t_{j+1}, in reverse order. Specialize the proof of pathcalc01 Section 4. The detour Q from t_{j+1} back to t_j is the single ordinary edge t_{j+1}t_j. The two join triples required to close P_j with this edge are (a_j,t_{j+1},t_j) and (t_{j+1},t_j,b_j). If the first is non-tight, boundary antisymmetry gives its reverse (t_j,t_{j+1},a_j), outcome (1). If the second is non-tight, its reverse (b_j,t_j,t_{j+1}) is tight, outcome (2). If both are tight, the cyclic word (t_{j+1},t_j,b_j,...,a_j) has every cyclic consecutive triple tight, giving outcome (3). No cyclic permutation of an ordered triple is used.

                    • [insertions_create_antipodal_commoncore_twocovers] Three successful transferred-label insertions create antipodal common-core two-covers
                        STATEMENT
                        Assume the all-equal support-triangle setting and suppose, for every i modulo three, the transferred label t_{i+2} is insertable into P_i=(t_i,M_i,t_{i+1}). Put T={t_1,t_2,t_3}. Then H[M_i union T] is Hamiltonian for each i. Consequently, for every permutation {i,j,k}={1,2,3}, the proper subtournament U_k=H-M_k is non-Hamiltonian of path-cover number two and has the two explicit two-covers (M_i union T)|M_j and M_i|(M_j union T). Thus the all-three-insertable branch creates an antipodal common-core support switch in which the entire three-label set T moves from one core to the other.
                        BODY / PROOF
                        Inserting t_{i+2} into P_i produces a Hamilton path R_i on S_i union {t_{i+2}}. Since S_i=V(A_i) union {t_{i+1}}=M_i union {t_i,t_{i+1}}, its support is exactly M_i union T. Fix distinct i,j,k. The sets M_i union T and M_j are disjoint and cover V(H)-M_k, so R_i|M_j is a two-cover of U_k=H-M_k. Similarly M_i|R_j is a two-cover of U_k. The subtournament U_k cannot be Hamiltonian, because M_k is itself a tight path and a Hamilton path on U_k together with M_k would give a spanning two-cover of H, contradicting pc(H)>2. Hence pc(U_k)=2. Their common cores are M_i,M_j, while all three labels in T lie on the first core in one cover and on the second core in the other.

                      • [disagreement_to_an_endpoint_edge_or_a_fullsupport_tight_cycle] Successful insertion localizes order disagreement to an endpoint edge or a full-support tight cycle
                          STATEMENT
                          Assume the all-three-successful-insertion branch of 1278e049ce8e. Then there exist distinct indices i,j modulo three such that the successful-insertion path R_j on M_j union T orders t_{i+1} before t_i, opposite to P_i=(t_i,M_i,t_{i+1}). Since V(R_j) intersect V(P_i)={t_i,t_{i+1}}, the reversed-order path-intersection argument applied to P_i and R_j localizes at the two endpoint edges of P_i: either there is a tight triple reversing one of the displayed endpoint edges of P_i, or there is a vertex-simple tight cycle whose vertex set contains all of V(P_i). In the latter case, if the R_j subpath from t_{i+1} to t_i has an interior vertex, the cycle support properly contains V(P_i) and hence is a Hamiltonian enlargement of S_i.
                          BODY / PROOF
                          Every R_j is a total order on T={t_1,t_2,t_3} and preserves t_j before t_{j+1}. No total order can simultaneously satisfy the three cyclic inequalities t_1<t_2, t_2<t_3, t_3<t_1. Hence R_j reverses at least one other cyclic pair, say it places t_{i+1} before t_i. The supports of P_i and R_j meet exactly in {t_i,t_{i+1}} because their non-T petals M_i and M_j are disjoint. Apply Section 4 of pathcalc01 with P=P_i and Q=R_j. The two common vertices are the two ends v_0=t_i and v_k=t_{i+1} of P_i and occur oppositely on Q. In the proof of pathcalc01 the only possible reversing triples are therefore the endpoint-local triples based on (v_0,v_1) or (v_{k-1},v_k). If neither reversal occurs, the proof constructs a tight cycle by following the Q-subpath from v_k to v_0 and then P from v_0 through v_{k-1} back to v_k; this cycle contains every vertex of P_i. If the Q-subpath has an interior vertex then the cycle support strictly contains V(P_i), and cutting the cycle at any place gives a tight Hamilton path on that larger support.

                        • [cycle_branch_gives_two_opposite_nearhamiltonian_truncations] The full-support cycle branch gives two opposite near-Hamiltonian truncations
                            STATEMENT
                            Continue b2f0a8047d8d in its cycle branch. Let P_i=(t_i,M_i,t_{i+1}) and let the chosen successful-insertion path R_j have the decomposition R_j=L,t_{i+1},E^o,t_i,R, where L and R are the maximal prefix and suffix outside the reversed endpoint segment E=(t_{i+1},E^o,t_i). If the path-intersection proof closes to a tight cycle C consisting of E followed by P_i from t_i back to t_{i+1}, then both induced subtournaments U-L and U-R are Hamiltonian, where U=V(P_i) union V(R_j). Moreover L and R are both nonempty whenever H[U] is non-Hamiltonian. In the all-equal insertion setting U=H-M_k for the remaining petal k, so this gives two opposite proper Hamiltonian truncations of the non-Hamiltonian path-cover-two subtournament H-M_k.
                            BODY / PROOF
                            The cycle order is t_{i+1},E^o,t_i,M_i,t_{i+1}. To absorb the prefix L, cut this cycle immediately before t_{i+1} and prepend the inherited R_j-prefix L. The join into t_{i+1} and the first edge of E is inherited from R_j, while the remainder follows the tight cycle, so L followed by the cycle-without-repeat is a Hamilton path on U-R. Dually, rotate the cycle so that it ends at t_i and append the inherited suffix R; the final join through t_i into the first vertex of R is inherited from R_j, giving a Hamilton path on U-L. If R were empty, the first construction would Hamiltonize all of U; if L were empty, the second would Hamiltonize all of U. Hence for non-Hamiltonian U both are nonempty. In the all-equal insertion setting V(P_i) union V(R_j)=M_i union M_j union T=H-M_k.

                          • [reversing_triple_the_cycle_alternative_is_impossible] Successful insertion forces an endpoint-edge reversing triple; the cycle alternative is impossible
                              STATEMENT
                              Assume the all-three-successful-insertion branch of 1278e049ce8e. Then for some i there is a tight triple that reverses one of the two displayed endpoint edges of P_i=(t_i,M_i,t_{i+1}). In particular the order disagreement from e677f3148059 can, in this branch, always be localized to a component-end edge; the full-support tight-cycle alternative of b2f0a8047d8d never occurs.
                              BODY / PROOF
                              Fix any j and let R_j be obtained by inserting t_{j+2} into P_j=(t_j,M_j,t_{j+1}). If the inserted t_{j+2} occurs before the terminal t_{j+1}, then R_j orders t_{j+2} before t_{j+1}, opposite to P_{j+1}, which orders t_{j+1} before t_{j+2}. Apply b2f0a8047d8d with i=j+1. In the decomposition of c36d628fe858, the reversed R_j-segment from t_{j+2} to t_{j+1} ends at the terminal vertex of R_j, so its exterior suffix R is empty. The cycle branch is impossible because c36d628fe858 would then Hamiltonize U=H-M_j, contradicting the known non-Hamiltonicity of that subtournament. Hence an endpoint-edge reversing triple is forced. Dually, if t_{j+2} occurs after the initial t_j, then R_j orders t_j before t_{j+2}, opposite to P_{j+2}, which orders t_{j+2} before t_j. Apply b2f0a8047d8d with i=j+2. Now the reversed segment begins at the initial vertex of R_j, so the exterior prefix L is empty, again excluding the cycle branch by c36d628fe858. Every insertion position is either before t_{j+1} or after t_j (indeed an internal insertion satisfies both), so one of the two arguments always applies.

                        • [insertion_forces_an_endpointedge_reversing_triple] Successful transferred-label insertion forces an endpoint-edge reversing triple
                            STATEMENT
                            Assume the all-three-successful-insertion branch of 1278e049ce8e. Then the cycle alternative of b2f0a8047d8d cannot occur. Consequently some successful-insertion path and some displayed support path P_i force a tight triple reversing one of the two displayed endpoint edges of P_i. Thus the successful-insertion arm reaches the endpoint-edge-reversal interface directly, strictly sharpening bare relative-order disagreement.
                            BODY / PROOF
                            Choose j and a cyclic pair reversed by R_j relative to a different P_i, as in b2f0a8047d8d. It is enough to choose a reversed pair whose oriented R_j-segment reaches an endpoint of R_j. This is always possible. If t_{j+2} is inserted before t_j, use the reversed pair (t_{j+1},t_{j+2}) relative to P_{j+1}; the R_j segment from t_{j+2} to t_{j+1} is all of R_j. If t_{j+2} is inserted after t_{j+1}, use the reversed pair (t_{j+2},t_j) relative to P_{j+2}; the segment from t_j to t_{j+2} is all of R_j. If the insertion is strictly between t_j and t_{j+1}, write R_j=(t_j,L,t_{j+2},R,t_{j+1}) in block notation and use the reversed pair (t_{j+1},t_{j+2}) relative to P_{j+1}; its reversed R_j-segment E runs from t_{j+2} through R to the terminal vertex t_{j+1}. Apply the reversed-order path-intersection proof from pathcalc01 to P_i and R_j. If it yields an endpoint-edge reversing triple, we are done. Otherwise it closes E together with P_i into a tight cycle C. In the first two endpoint-insertion cases C contains all of R_j. In the internal case, rotate C so that it starts at t_{j+2} and ends at t_{j+1}, then prepend the inherited R_j prefix (t_j,L): the only join triples are already consecutive triples of R_j, so this gives a Hamilton path on U=V(P_i) union V(R_j). In every case U=H-M_k for the remaining petal k. Since M_k is a tight path, Hamiltonicity of U would give a spanning two-cover U|M_k of H, contradiction. Hence the cycle alternative is impossible and the endpoint-edge reversing triple is forced.

                          • [insertions_force_endpoint_reversals_on_at_least_two_supports] Successful transferred-label insertions force endpoint reversals on at least two supports
                              STATEMENT
                              In the all-three-successful-insertion branch, at least two distinct displayed support paths P_i receive a tight triple reversing one of their two endpoint edges. More precisely, every cyclic transferred-label pair whose order is reversed by some R_j relative to P_i yields an endpoint-edge reversing triple for P_i, and the set of reversed cyclic pairs covers at least two of the three P_i.
                              BODY / PROOF
                              For each j classify the insertion of t_{j+2} into P_j by L, M, or R according as it lies before t_j, strictly between t_j and t_{j+1}, or after t_{j+1}. The induced order on T={t_1,t_2,t_3} shows: type L reverses exactly the cyclic pair of P_{j+1}; type M reverses the cyclic pairs of both P_{j+1} and P_{j+2}; type R reverses exactly the cyclic pair of P_{j+2}. For any such reversed pair, apply the path-intersection argument exactly as in d6b6225e634c. In types L and R the reversed R_j segment is all of R_j; in type M the segment for P_{j+1} reaches the terminal endpoint of R_j and the segment for P_{j+2} reaches the initial endpoint. Hence in every case the cycle alternative can be completed with the remaining prefix or suffix of R_j to Hamiltonize U=H-M_k, contradicting that M_k is a tight complementary path in a counterexample. Therefore every reversed cyclic pair yields an endpoint-edge reversing triple on the corresponding P_i. Finally P_i fails to receive any reversed pair only if the source insertion R_{i-1} is type R and R_{i-2} is type L. Two distinct indices cannot both satisfy this condition, since their requirements assign conflicting L and R types to a common source insertion. Thus at most one P_i escapes, and at least two distinct support paths receive endpoint-edge reversals.

                        • [reversal_all_three_transferredlabel_insertions_are_internal] Without an endpoint-edge reversal, all three transferred-label insertions are internal
                            STATEMENT
                            Assume the all-three-successful-insertion branch of 1278e049ce8e. If the endpoint-edge-reversal alternative of b2f0a8047d8d does not occur, then for every j modulo three the successful insertion of t_{j+2} into P_j=(t_j,M_j,t_{j+1}) lies strictly between t_j and t_{j+1}; in particular it is neither before t_j nor after t_{j+1}. Thus the reversal-free successful-insertion residue consists of three genuine internal insertion gaps, one in each M_j corridor.
                            BODY / PROOF
                            Fix j. Suppose first that t_{j+2} is inserted before t_j, so R_j=(t_{j+2},t_j,M_j,t_{j+1}) in block notation. Then R_j reverses the cyclic pair t_{j+1},t_{j+2} relative to P_{j+1}=(t_{j+1},M_{j+1},t_{j+2}). Apply b2f0a8047d8d with i=j+1. By hypothesis its endpoint-edge-reversal alternative is absent, so its tight-cycle alternative occurs. Here the R_j subpath from t_{j+2} to t_{j+1} is all of R_j, hence the resulting tight cycle has support T union V(M_j) union V(M_{j+1}). Opening that cycle gives a Hamilton path on this support. The complementary vertex set is exactly V(M_{j+2}), which is already a tight path. These two paths span H, contradiction. Dually, if t_{j+2} is inserted after t_{j+1}, then R_j reverses the pair t_{j+2},t_j relative to P_{j+2}; applying b2f0a8047d8d with i=j+2 again makes the cycle support all of T union V(M_j) union V(M_{j+2}), whose complement M_{j+1} is a tight path, giving a spanning two-cover. Hence neither endpoint insertion is possible. Applying this for all j proves the claim.

                      • [the_antipodal_switch_by_a_fourstate_singletontransfer_corridor] Successful transferred-label insertions fill the antipodal switch by a four-state singleton-transfer corridor
                          STATEMENT
                          Assume the all-three-successful-insertion branch of 1278e049ce8e. Fix cyclic indices i,i+1,i+2 and put T={t_i,t_{i+1},t_{i+2}} and U=H-M_{i+2}. Then U has four two-covers
                          M_i | (M_{i+1} union T),
                          (A_i) | S_{i+1},
                          S_i | (M_{i+1},t_{i+2}),
                          (M_i union T) | M_{i+1},
                          where A_i=(t_i,M_i), S_i=(t_i,M_i,t_{i+1}), S_{i+1}=(t_{i+1},M_{i+1},t_{i+2}), and the first and last mixed supports are the successful-insertion Hamiltonian supports M_{i+1} union T and M_i union T. Consecutive covers differ by moving exactly one transferred label from the right support to the left, in the order t_i,t_{i+1},t_{i+2}. Thus the antipodal support switch of 1278e049ce8e is filled by a four-state singleton-transfer corridor.
                          BODY / PROOF
                          By 1278e049ce8e, M_i union T and M_{i+1} union T are Hamiltonian. The inherited paths M_i,M_{i+1}, A_i=(t_i,M_i), S_i=(t_i,M_i,t_{i+1}), S_{i+1}=(t_{i+1},M_{i+1},t_{i+2}), and (M_{i+1},t_{i+2}) are all tight from the base, support-triangle, and antipodal cube covers. Hence each displayed pair is a two-cover of U=H-M_{i+2}. The subtournament U is non-Hamiltonian because M_{i+2} is a tight path and a Hamilton path on U together with M_{i+2} would two-cover H. Comparing successive support partitions shows that the first move transfers only t_i, the second only t_{i+1}, and the third only t_{i+2}, always from the right support to the left while the M_i and M_{i+1} cores remain fixed.

                  • [allequal_barrier_geometry_has_a_rigid_ninelabel_endpoint_shell] The all-equal barrier geometry has a rigid nine-label endpoint shell
                      STATEMENT
                      In the all-equal endpoint-barrier branch, put Omega={t_i,b_i,a_i : i=1,2,3}. Then all nine labels are distinct. For indices modulo three, E_i={b_{i+1},a_{i+1},t_{i+2},a_{i+2}}. Hence the six natural endpoint supports L_i={t_i,b_i} union E_i and R_i={a_i,t_{i+1}} union E_i satisfy L_i=Omega-{a_i,t_{i+1},b_{i+2}} and R_i={a_1,a_2,a_3} union {t_{i+1},b_{i+1},t_{i+2}}. Consequently the three omitted triples Omega-L_i are pairwise disjoint and partition Omega, while R_1,R_2,R_3 have common intersection {a_1,a_2,a_3} and pairwise intersections {a_1,a_2,a_3,t_j} for the appropriate transferred label t_j. This is a purely set-theoretic shell description; no Hamiltonicity of the six supports is asserted.
                      BODY / PROOF
                      In a minimum counterexample the all-equal cube has n=3r>10, hence r>=4. Thus each M_i has order r-1>=3, so t_i,b_i,a_i are distinct within A_i, and different A_i are disjoint. Therefore Omega has order nine. By definition, E_i consists of the displayed endpoints of M_{i+1} and A_{i+2}; these are b_{i+1},a_{i+1},t_{i+2},a_{i+2}. Substitution gives L_i={t_i,b_i} union E_i=Omega-{a_i,t_{i+1},b_{i+2}} and R_i={a_i,t_{i+1}} union E_i={a_1,a_2,a_3} union {t_{i+1},b_{i+1},t_{i+2}}. The omitted triples Omega-L_i use each a-label, t-label and b-label exactly once as i varies, so they partition Omega. The common-core and pairwise-intersection formulas for the R_i follow immediately. The earlier Hamiltonicity assertion depended on 3ed34cc96c0d and is intentionally removed.

              • [nonuniform_neutral_transport_or_certified_order_disagreement] The {1,1,1} cube reduces to strict descent, nonuniform neutral transport, or certified order disagreement
                  STATEMENT
                  Let Gamma be a minimum-span cyclic defect certificate of run type {1,1,1}, with base component-order profile g. Then exactly one of the following structural regimes applies. (1) Some pair of entries of g differs by at least two, and one canonical cube state has strictly smaller quadratic potential than the antipodal base states. (2) The profile is equitable but nonuniform, and the two antipodal equal-profile states are joined inside the cube by the certified three-step Phi-neutral singleton-transfer path of 5ba8c8a53ce9. (3) The profile is all equal, and the antipodal support triangle forces certified relative-order disagreement by e677f3148059. Thus the all-equal {1,1,1} residue is no longer a separate unresolved local geometry; only the nonuniform neutral-transport regime remains to be consumed by the standard terminal-frontier machinery when strict descent is excluded.
                  BODY / PROOF
                  By f3965b3ddf4e, the six nonconstant cube states are exactly the six ordered singleton transfers of g. If a pair of base orders differs by at least two, transferring one vertex from the larger to the smaller strictly decreases Phi, giving (1). Otherwise g is equitable. If it is not all equal, 5ba8c8a53ce9 gives the stated three-step Phi-neutral path between antipodes, giving (2). If all three base orders are equal, the canonical antipodal exchange has the support-triangle structure used in e677f3148059, whose certified conclusion is unavoidable relative-order disagreement, giving (3). These cases exhaust all integer triples g.

                • [cube111terminalclosure01] At a trapped quadratic minimum the {1,1,1} cube already yields a canonical closure input
                    STATEMENT
                    Let H be a minimum counterexample and suppose a minimum-span cyclic defect certificate of run type {1,1,1} yields a three-cover C in a trapped pairwise-repartition component, with C minimizing the quadratic potential Phi in that component. Then H exposes one of the canonical theorem-closure inputs listed in c195f52d5b31: a proper Hamiltonian four- or five-vertex support with path-cover-two complement, an explicit cross triple or interval connector, order disagreement, an inherited displayed-path edge whose endpoints are separated by a comparison cover, a leave-and-return excursion through another displayed core, crossing multiplicity at least three, a bounded local defect-compression obstruction, or a reversed join. In particular, no {1,1,1} cyclic-defect state can remain as a structureless terminal Phi-minimum.
                    BODY / PROOF
                    Apply c195f52d5b31 directly to C. Its hypotheses are exactly the present ones: H is a minimum counterexample and C is a spanning three-cover minimizing the quadratic potential in a trapped connected component of the pairwise-repartition graph. Therefore H has one of the listed outcomes: a proper Hamiltonian four- or five-vertex support with path-cover-two complement, an explicit cross triple or interval connector, order disagreement, an inherited displayed-path edge separated by a comparison cover, a leave-and-return excursion through another displayed core, crossing multiplicity at least three, a bounded local defect-compression obstruction, or a reversed join.
                    
                    Thus the {1,1,1} state cannot remain without one of those outcomes. ∎

              • [orderfifteen_cubeescape_specialization] Order-fifteen cube-escape specialization
                  STATEMENT
                  Organizational branch for the r=5 / order-15 specialization of the all-equal cube, separating order-specific escape arguments from the general four-side complement theorem.
                  BODY / PROOF
                  This branch contains order-15 specializations only. General four-side and barrier lemmas remain reusable premises via dependency edges rather than reasoning parentage.

                • [from_the_allequal_barrier_branch_escapes_the_canonical_cube] At order fifteen every four-side descent from the all-equal barrier branch escapes the canonical cube
                    STATEMENT
                    Assume the all-equal {1,1,1} barrier branch with r=5, so |V(H)|=15. Fix one canonical mixed four-path Q_i=(b_i,t_i,t_{i+2},a_{i+1}) from 2bac72daae4a, and choose a two-cover P|R of H-V(Q_i). Suppose its component orders are 6 and 5. Apply foursidedescentobstruction to Q_i|P|R. If its strict-descent alternative occurs, the resulting spanning three-cover has profile 5|5|5 and is not one of the eight canonical cube covers. Thus at order fifteen the four-side descent alternative is a genuine escape from the {1,1,1} cube, never a recurrence inside it.
                    BODY / PROOF
                    Write Q_i=(x_0,x_1,x_2,x_3)=(b_i,t_i,t_{i+2},a_{i+1}) and P=(p_1,...,p_6). Every strict descent in the proof of foursidedescentobstruction replaces Q_i|P by one of four 5|5 repartitions: (a) (Q_i union {p_1}) | (P-{p_1}); (b) (Q_i union {p_6}) | (P-{p_6}); (c) F_L | (M union {x_3}), where F_L={x_0,x_1,x_2,p_1,p_6}; or (d) F_R | (M union {x_0}), where F_R={x_1,x_2,x_3,p_1,p_6} and M=(p_2,...,p_5). Together with the untouched five-path R, each gives profile 5|5|5. In the {1,1,1} cube only the three transferred boundary labels t_1,t_2,t_3 move across cuts; each core M_j stays intact inside a single cube component. Hence any canonical cube component containing a vertex of M_j contains the whole four-vertex core M_j. In cases (a),(b), the new five-side contains both b_i in M_i and a_{i+1} in M_{i+1}, so it mixes two distinct fixed cores and cannot be a cube component. In case (c), F_L contains b_i in M_i and the two transferred labels t_i,t_{i+2}; only two further vertices remain, so F_L cannot contain all four vertices of M_i and therefore cannot be a cube component. The same argument for a_{i+1} in M_{i+1} excludes F_R in case (d). Thus every descended 5|5|5 cover lies outside the canonical eight-state cube.

                  • [nodescent_fourside_branch_also_escapes_the_canonical_cube] The order-fifteen no-descent four-side branch also escapes the canonical cube
                      STATEMENT
                      Assume the order-15 all-equal barrier setting of d3a358471810, with Q_i=(x_0,x_1,x_2,x_3)=(b_i,t_i,t_{i+2},a_{i+1}) and a complementary 6|5 cover P|R, where P=(p_1,...,p_6). Suppose the strict-descent alternative of foursidedescentobstruction does not occur. Then there is nevertheless a legal repartition of Q_i|P into two Hamiltonian five-sets whose resulting spanning 5|5|5 cover lies outside all eight canonical {1,1,1} cube states. Hence at order fifteen the entire four-side barrier branch, descent or no descent, forces genuine escape from the canonical cube.
                      BODY / PROOF
                      In the no-descent branch of foursidedescentobstruction, M=(p_2,p_3,p_4,p_5) satisfies H[M union {x_0}] and H[M union {x_3}] non-Hamiltonian, while the crossed five-set A=F_L={x_0,x_1,x_2,p_1,p_6} is Hamiltonian. Its complementary five-set F=M union {x_3} is non-Hamiltonian. Apply the certified order-ten exchange-matrix theorem in extremal01 to the partition A|F. For a in A and y in F, write X_{a,y}=(A-{a}) union {y} and Y_{a,y}=(F-{y}) union {a}. Every column y has at least three X-good cells and every row a has at least four Y-good cells. Hence there are at least ten double-good cells. We claim some double-good cell has a not in {x_1,x_2}={t_i,t_{i+2}}. Otherwise, in each of the other three rows a not in {x_1,x_2}, at least four cells are Y-good but none is X-good, giving at least 12 X-bad cells. Yet every one of the five columns has at least three X-good cells, so each column has at most two X-bad cells and the whole matrix has at most 10 X-bad cells, contradiction. Choose a double-good cell with a not in {x_1,x_2}. Then X_{a,y} is a Hamiltonian five-set retaining both transferred labels t_i,t_{i+2}, and Y_{a,y} is its Hamiltonian complement inside Q_i union P. Thus X_{a,y}|Y_{a,y}|R is a spanning 5|5|5 cover. By f3965b3ddf4e, the only canonical cube states with profile 5|5|5 are the two antipodes. In either antipode every component consists of one intact four-vertex core M_j together with exactly one transferred label. Since X_{a,y} contains two distinct transferred labels, it cannot be a component of either antipodal cover. Therefore the new 5|5|5 cover lies outside the canonical eight-state cube.

          • [cubeendpointdisturbance_recomp01] The {1,1,1} cube reduces to descent, neutral transport, or all-equal endpoint disturbance
              STATEMENT
              Let Gamma be a minimum-span cyclic defect certificate of run type {1,1,1}. Then either: (1) some cube state has strictly smaller quadratic potential; (2) the equitable nonuniform antipodes are joined inside the cube by a three-step Phi-neutral singleton-transfer path; or (3) the antipodal base cover is all equal, A|B|C with |A|=|B|=|C|=r, and for each base path X in {A,B,C}, arbitrary two-covers of the two endpoint deletions of X force at least one standard endpoint-transport disturbance: order disagreement, inherited-edge support crossing, or a leave-and-return excursion relative to A|B|C. Moreover, whenever opposite endpoint probes of a displayed path preserve the surviving inherited block intact and in inherited order and have no order disagreement, the common-middle square machinery yields either a Hamiltonian support of order r+2 or a doubled same-side reverse obstruction.
              BODY / PROOF
              The cube-size parametrization and transfer classification give the three cases. If the size profile has a gap at least two, transferring one vertex from a largest class to a smallest class strictly decreases Phi. If the profile is equitable but nonuniform, the certified neutral-transfer lemma supplies the three-step Phi-neutral path between antipodes. The only remaining case is the all-equal profile.
              
              In the all-equal case, apply the certified equal-cover endpoint-probe theorem independently to A, B, and C. For any chosen base path X and arbitrary two-covers of its two endpoint deletions, one obtains order disagreement, inherited-edge support crossing, or a leave-and-return excursion relative to the inherited three-cover. Thus the all-equal case is already an endpoint-disturbance source on each of its three base paths.
              
              Separately, suppose opposite endpoint probes of some displayed path satisfy the stronger intact-block hypotheses and have no order disagreement. The opposite-end migration lemma gives the two-for-two support migration; the common-middle closure lemma completes the four-corner square; and the square-amplification theorem yields either a Hamiltonian support of order r+2 or the doubled same-side reverse obstruction. This last implication is conditional and is not obtained by negating the endpoint-disturbance theorem.

          • [of_a_threeisolateddefect_cube_state_is_a_onesided_slide] Every interface of a three-isolated-defect cube state is a one-sided slide
              STATEMENT
              Let Gamma be a minimum-span cyclic defect certificate of run type {1,1,1}, and let A|B|C be any of its eight cyclic-interval three-covers. At each of the three displayed cyclic interfaces, exactly one of the two join triples is non-tight and the other is tight. Hence every interface is the single-tight slide alternative of the three-block interface trichotomy. In particular, if A|B|C minimizes Phi in its trapped contiguous-block relocation component and two adjacent displayed blocks X,Y satisfy |X|>=|Y|+2, then the interface slide must transfer one endpoint vertex from Y into X; the opposite transfer would strictly decrease Phi.
              BODY / PROOF
              Each displayed cut of a cube state is one selected endpoint of one isolated defect edge of Gamma. Since Gamma is a matching, exactly one of the two cyclic defect edges incident with that cut is present: the chosen isolated defect edge; the other incident cyclic edge is nondefective. These two incident cyclic defect tests are precisely the two join triples at the corresponding interface of the cyclic-interval cover. Thus exactly one join triple is non-tight and one is tight, so the local interface trichotomy is always its cut-slide alternative. Now suppose the state is Phi-minimal in its trapped relocation component and |X|>=|Y|+2. Sliding one vertex from X to Y changes Phi by 2(|Y|-|X|)+2<0, impossible. Therefore the actual one-sided slide at that interface must be the reverse direction, moving an endpoint of the smaller block Y into the larger block X.

          • [three_isolated_cyclic_defects_in_every_spanthree_ordering] Path-cover number above two forbids three isolated cyclic defects in every span-three ordering
              STATEMENT
              Let H be any boundary tournament with pc(H)>2, and let pi=(v_1,...,v_n) be a spanning ordering of defect span three. Then the cyclic defect graph associated with pi cannot have run type {1,1,1}. Thus exclusion of the three-isolated-defect geometry uses only pc(H)>2; no minimum-order hypothesis is required.
              BODY / PROOF
              Let i be the leftmost defect center and put x=v_{i+1}, P=(v_1,...,v_i), Q=(v_{i+2},...,v_n). Because every defect center lies among i,i+1,i+2, every consecutive triple internal to P or Q is tight, so H-x=P|Q. Since pc(H)>2, the two outer joins through x are defective: if either were tight, x could be absorbed into the corresponding path and the other path would give a two-cover.
              
              Form the cyclic defect graph Gamma of the cyclic order P,x,Q. The three path boundaries of P|{x}|Q form a vertex cover of Gamma, so tau(Gamma)<=3. If tau(Gamma)<=2, cutting at such a cover gives a two-cover of H by cyclic tight intervals, contrary to pc(H)>2. Hence tau(Gamma)=3.
              
              Suppose Gamma had run type {1,1,1}. By 2923b2b2b233 its eight minimum cut sets form the full three-cube of three-covers, and by 810c33003128 their component orders have the form s_j=g_j+x_{j+1}-x_j cyclically. Choose the zero state to be the displayed singleton lift P|{x}|Q. One component then has order g_j=1. Set x_j=1 and x_{j+1}=0, leaving the third bit arbitrary. The formula gives s_j=0, contradicting that every cube state is a three-cover with nonempty components. Therefore Gamma is not {1,1,1}.

            • [both_cyclic_orientations_whenever_pathcover_number_exceeds_two] Every three-cover with long components has barriers in both cyclic orientations whenever path-cover number exceeds two
                STATEMENT
                Let H be any boundary tournament with pc(H)>2 and let A|B|C be a three-cover with |A|,|B|,|C|>=3. For an ordered interface X|Y, call it a barrier when both join triples needed to concatenate X followed by Y are non-tight. Each of the two cyclic orientations A->B->C->A and A->C->B->A contains a barrier. Consequently there are two directed barrier interfaces, one from each orientation cycle; after relabeling they are opposite orientations of one unordered pair, share a source, or share a target.
                BODY / PROOF
                Consider the cyclic orientation A->B->C->A. At any interface, the two join triples cannot both be tight, because then the two adjacent displayed paths concatenate and, together with the third path, give a two-cover of H. Suppose this cyclic orientation had no barrier. Then every one of its three interfaces has exactly one non-tight join triple. Since all three displayed paths have order at least three, these three defects are separated around the cyclic order by tight internal triples. The cyclic defect graph therefore has run type {1,1,1}. Cutting the cyclic order at an internal tight location gives a spanning ordering of defect span three with the same three isolated cyclic defects, contradicting 33b80d34aad4. Hence this orientation contains a barrier.
                
                The same argument applied to A->C->B->A gives a barrier in the reverse orientation cycle. The two directed edge sets are disjoint; any choice of one directed edge from each has, after relabeling, one of the three stated incidence types.

            • [a_central_fiveset_an_outer_fiveset_or_two_opposite_foursets] Every deletion two-cover in a tournament with path-cover number above two yields a central five-set, an outer five-set, or two opposite four-sets
                STATEMENT
                Let H be a boundary tournament with pc(H)>2 and let H-x=P|Q be a deletion two-cover, where P=(p_0,...,p_m), Q=(q_0,...,q_s), and |P|,|Q|>=3. Then at least one of the following holds: (1) (q_1,q_0,x,p_m,p_{m-1}) is a tight five-path; (2) (p_1,p_0,x,q_s,q_{s-1}) is a tight five-path; (3) both (p_1,p_0,q_s,q_{s-1}) and (q_1,q_0,p_m,p_{m-1}) are tight four-paths. If neither five-set in (1) and (2) is Hamiltonian, then both cross triples (p_m,x,q_0) and (q_s,x,p_0) are tight and outcome (3) holds. If H is a minimum counterexample, every proper Hamiltonian support displayed above has non-Hamiltonian complement of path-cover number two; and if |P|,|Q|>=4, the two four-sets in (3) are disjoint.
                BODY / PROOF
                Because H has no two-cover, (p_{m-1},p_m,x) and (x,q_0,q_1) are non-tight: otherwise x can be absorbed into P or Q. Boundary antisymmetry therefore gives (x,p_m,p_{m-1}) and (q_1,q_0,x) tight. If (p_m,x,q_0) is non-tight, then (q_0,x,p_m) is tight and (q_1,q_0,x,p_m,p_{m-1}) is a tight five-path, giving (1).
                
                Assume (p_m,x,q_0) is tight. At least one of the two wrap triples at Q|P is non-tight, since if both were tight then QP|{x} would two-cover H. If exactly one wrap triple were non-tight, the two forced defects adjacent to x together with that wrap defect would form three isolated cyclic defects in the span-three ordering P,x,Q, contradicting 33b80d34aad4. Hence both wrap triples are non-tight, and their reversal mates give the tight four-path (p_1,p_0,q_s,q_{s-1}).
                
                Also (p_1,p_0,x) and (x,q_s,q_{s-1}) are tight, since the opposite orientations would again absorb x into P or Q. Exactly one of (p_0,x,q_s) and (q_s,x,p_0) is tight. In the first case (p_1,p_0,x,q_s,q_{s-1}) is a tight five-path, giving (2). In the second case the reverse cross (q_s,x,p_0) is tight. Apply the preceding central-tight argument to the swapped deletion order Q,x,P; it gives the opposite tight four-path (q_1,q_0,p_m,p_{m-1}), hence (3).
                
                If both five-sets are non-Hamiltonian, the first branch is impossible, so (p_m,x,q_0) is tight; the second five-path branch is also impossible, so (q_s,x,p_0) is tight, and the preceding argument gives both four-paths. For a minimum counterexample, the complement conclusion follows from mincex01. Disjointness for component orders at least four is immediate from the displayed endpoint pairs.

        • [cyclic_defect_rotation_route] Cyclic defect rotation route
            STATEMENT
            For a spanning ordering of minimum defect span three, use the certified reverse cyclic endpoint hook to define a rotation that moves one endpoint across the cyclic cut while preserving span at most three. Conjecture that iterating canonical such rotations either produces defect span at most two or forces a repeated cyclic state whose accumulated reversal data yields a tight cycle/path splice closing the theorem.
            BODY / PROOF
            The new ingredient is to use the cyclic closure of a span-three ordering as the state space rather than a fixed linear defect window. The endpoint hook guarantees a local direction to rotate; the challenge is to find a global progress or recurrence certificate.

        • [proper_cyclic_defect_certificate_has_a_doublewrap_rotation] Every nonmatching proper cyclic defect certificate has a double-wrap rotation
            STATEMENT
            Let H be a minimum counterexample and let pi be a minimum-defect-span-three ordering with proper cyclic defect graph Gamma. If Gamma is not the three-edge matching of run type {1,1,1}, then the same cyclic vertex order admits a cut q with nu(Gamma-q)=2 such that both cyclic defect edges incident with q are present. Consequently the corresponding rotation has contiguous-path number three, both wrap triples are non-tight, S=(v_2,v_1,v_n,v_{n-1}) is a tight four-path, and pc(H-S)=2. Thus among the five proper cyclic run geometries, {1,1,1} is the only one that cannot be represented in double-wrap form.
            BODY / PROOF
            By the certified five-type classification, the non-{1,1,1} proper run multisets are {2,1,1}, {3,1}, {3,2}, and {5}. In each case choose q to be a degree-two vertex of a nontrivial defect run so that deleting q leaves matching number two: for {2,1,1}, take the middle vertex of the 2-run, leaving the two singleton edges; for {3,1}, take an internal vertex of the 3-run adjacent to an end of that run, leaving one end edge of the 3-run together with the singleton; for {3,2}, take the middle vertex of the 2-run, leaving the 3-run, whose matching number is two; for {5}, take the second vertex of the 5-run from one end, leaving a 3-run, again of matching number two. Hence in every case nu(Gamma-q)=2, so the cyclic defect identity gives contiguous-path number c(pi_q)=1+nu(Gamma-q)=3. Because q is incident with two defect edges of Gamma, those two edges are exactly the two wrap tests in the linear rotation pi_q, so both wrap triples are non-tight. Boundary antisymmetry reverses them to tight triples (v_1,v_n,v_{n-1}) and (v_2,v_1,v_n), yielding the tight four-path S=(v_2,v_1,v_n,v_{n-1}). Finally S is a proper Hamiltonian support, and the minimum-counterexample calculus gives pc(H-S)=2.

          • [cyclic_nonmatching_fourwindow_transport01] Every nonmatching proper cyclic defect certificate reaches four-window transport
              STATEMENT
              Let H be a minimum counterexample and let pi be a minimum-defect-span-three ordering whose cyclic defect graph Gamma is proper and is not the three-edge matching of run type {1,1,1}. Then the connected cyclic-interval three-cover family determined by pi contains a cover W|R|S with W a Hamiltonian four-set and H-W=R|S a two-cover. Consequently either |V(H)|<=14, or that pairwise-repartition component contains a strict endpoint-transfer quadratic-potential descent from such a four-window state, or it contains the bounded path-cover-two transport package of four_window_transport_allorders01.
              BODY / PROOF
              By 687bbaa431c3, the same cyclic order has a double-wrap rotation with canonical tight four-path W and pc(H-W)=2. The three cyclic intervals of this rotation form one of the cyclic-interval three-covers associated with a minimum cut set of the same defect graph. By 5d81c7bd0407, all such cyclic-interval three-covers lie in one connected subgraph of the pairwise-repartition graph. Apply four_window_transport_allorders01 to W and a displayed two-cover R|S of H-W. Its three alternatives are exactly the asserted small-order, strict-descent, and bounded-transport outcomes. Thus deletion provenance is not essential: the mechanism belongs to every nonmatching proper cyclic defect certificate.

          • [every_deletion_singleton_lift_has_a_doublewrap_rotation] Every deletion singleton lift has a double-wrap rotation
              STATEMENT
              Let H be a minimum counterexample and let H-x=P|Q be any deletion two-cover. Form the spanning three-cover P|{x}|Q and concatenate its three displayed paths cyclically. Its cyclic defect graph Gamma has vertex-cover number exactly three. Moreover Gamma cannot have run type {1,1,1}. Consequently this cyclic order is a proper nonmatching minimum-span cyclic defect certificate, so by 687bbaa431c3 some rotation is a double-wrap span-three ordering with the canonical tight reversed four-path and two-cover complement supplied there.
              BODY / PROOF
              The three path boundaries of P|{x}|Q form a vertex cover of Gamma, so tau(Gamma)<=3. If tau(Gamma)<=2, cutting the cyclic ordering at at most two selected positions gives a spanning cover by at most two tight cyclic intervals, contradicting pc(H)>2. Hence tau(Gamma)=3. In particular, choosing any minimum vertex cover of Gamma and cutting there gives a spanning ordering of defect span three; since a counterexample admits no ordering of defect span at most two, this is a minimum-defect-span-three ordering. Since n>10 in a minimum counterexample and Gamma has a 3-vertex cover, Gamma is proper rather than the full cycle.
              
              Suppose Gamma had run type {1,1,1}. Then by the certified cube theorem 2923b2b2b233 all eight minimum vertex covers obtained by independently choosing one endpoint of each isolated defect edge give spanning three-covers, and by 810c33003128 their component orders satisfy s_i=g_i+x_{i+1}-x_i. Choose the reference endpoints so that the displayed singleton lift is the 000 state. Then one coordinate of g equals 1. Setting x_i=1 and x_{i+1}=0 for that coordinate (with the third bit arbitrary) gives another cube state whose corresponding path order is 0, contradicting that every cube state is a spanning three-cover. Thus Gamma is not {1,1,1}. The certified nonmatching cyclic theorem 687bbaa431c3 therefore supplies a double-wrap rotation and its canonical four-vertex support/complement structure.

            • [enters_fourside_descent_or_the_finite_pairedobstruction_menu] Every deletion state of order at least fifteen enters four-side descent or the finite paired-obstruction menu
                STATEMENT
                Let H be a minimum counterexample of order n>=15 and let H-x=P|Q be any deletion two-cover. Then there exists a spanning three-cover S|R|T with |S|=4 such that S is the canonical reversed four-path from a double-wrap rotation and H-S=R|T is a two-cover. One of R,T has order at least six. Consequently either a legal repartition of S with that long path strictly decreases quadratic potential, or the two displayed endpoints of S are simultaneously noninsertable into one common inherited middle path and hence realize one of the five outcomes of a8c9883902b1: a Hamiltonian four-set, the cyclic non-Hamiltonian four-kernel with universal one-vertex extension, a Hamiltonian five-set, a tight cross triple, or a direct tight interval connector.
                BODY / PROOF
                By 8ededbb50716, the singleton lift of the deletion cover has a double-wrap rotation. The certified double-wrap theorem 687bbaa431c3 supplies the tight reversed four-path S and, by minimum-counterexample calculus, pc(H-S)=2; choose a two-cover R|T. Since |R|+|T|=n-4>=11, one path, say R, has order at least six. Apply foursidedescentobstruction to S|R|T. Either one legal repartition of S|R strictly decreases Phi by 2|R|-10>0, or the two displayed endpoints of S are both noninsertable into the inherited middle path of R. In the latter case apply a8c9883902b1 to those two exterior vertices and that middle path, yielding its finite five-way menu.

              • [deletion_connector_only18] Above order seventeen the deletion-state paired-obstruction menu reduces to an interval connector or an opposite endpoint cross
                  STATEMENT
                  Let H be a minimum counterexample of order n>=18 and let H-x=P|Q be any deletion two-cover. Then the double-wrap four-side reduction of d26d8171978f yields either a legal strict quadratic-potential descent, explicit order disagreement, or one of the following two residual configurations. There is a tight four-path S=(u,a,b,v), a complementary two-cover H-S=R|T, and a long component R=(r_0,...,r_m) of order at least six, with inherited middle M=(r_1,...,r_{m-1}), such that either (A) for one of the two ordered endpoint pairs (s,t)=(u,v) or (v,u), there are indices 1<=i<j<=m-2 with j>=i+2 for which (s,r_{i+1},...,r_j,t) is a tight path; or (B) for some r_k in M the oppositely oriented endpoint cross (v,r_k,u) is tight. Thus, above order seventeen, the Hamiltonian four-set, cyclic four-kernel, Hamiltonian five-set, Hamiltonian six-set, and same-orientation endpoint-cross outputs are consumed; the only remaining paired-noninsertion outputs are a genuine interval connector or an endpoint cross opposite to the displayed orientation of S.
                  BODY / PROOF
                  Apply d26d8171978f. If its first alternative gives strict Phi descent, we are done. Otherwise the displayed endpoints u,v of its canonical tight four-path S=(u,a,b,v) are simultaneously noninsertable into the inherited middle path M of a complementary component R, and a8c9883902b1 gives one of five outcomes. If a Hamiltonian four-set occurs, minimum-counterexample calculus gives a non-Hamiltonian path-cover-two complement; 7bab8dd31d87 then gives strict descent, order disagreement, or a Hamiltonian six-set, and ham6_large_escape01 consumes the six-set for n>=18. If the exceptional cyclic non-Hamiltonian four-kernel occurs, adjoining any exterior vertex gives a proper Hamiltonian five-set by smallset01, and ham5_large_escape01 gives strict descent or order disagreement. A Hamiltonian five-set outcome is consumed directly by ham5_large_escape01. If the cross-triple outcome occurs, then for some r in M one of (u,r,v),(v,r,u) is tight. In the first case S=(u,a,b,v) and (u,r,v) are internally disjoint tight corridors with the same ordered endpoints, so 53d257fcf0a8 makes their five-vertex union Hamiltonian; its complement is non-Hamiltonian with path-cover number two, and ham5_large_escape01 again gives strict descent or order disagreement. In the second case the triple is oppositely oriented to the displayed endpoints of S and is retained as residual outcome (B); no reversal of S is asserted. Finally, the separated-pivot outcome of a8c9883902b1 is retained as residual outcome (A). Writing R=(r_0,...,r_m), its inherited middle is M=(r_1,...,r_{m-1}); translating the gap indices in M gives 1<=i<j<=m-2 with j>=i+2, and the connector is tight in one of the two endpoint orientations.

                • [deletion_state_escape18] Above order seventeen every deletion state enters strict quadratic descent or explicit order disagreement
                    STATEMENT
                    Let H be a minimum counterexample of order n>=18 and let H-x=P|Q be any one-vertex deletion two-cover. Then the pairwise-repartition component reached from its canonical double-wrap four-side state contains either a spanning three-cover of strictly smaller quadratic potential than that four-side state, or H contains explicit order disagreement. Equivalently, none of the five paired-noninsertion outputs of d26d8171978f remains a separate large-order obstruction.
                    BODY / PROOF
                    Apply d26d8171978f to the deletion two-cover H-x=P|Q. It supplies the canonical double-wrap spanning three-cover S|R|T, where S is a tight four-path and H-S=R|T is a two-cover.
                    
                    Since |R|+|T|=|V(H)|-4>=14, at least one of R,T has order at least seven. Relabel so |R|>=7.
                    
                    Apply the certified arbitrary-state theorem a25b748fb338 to the spanning three-cover S|R|T and the long path R. Either one legal repartition of S|R strictly decreases the quadratic potential from the canonical four-side state itself, or H contains explicit order disagreement.
                    
                    Thus the pairwise-repartition component containing the canonical double-wrap four-side state contains a strictly lower-Phi three-cover unless order disagreement already occurs. No paired-noninsertion, interval-connector, or opposite-endpoint-cross analysis is needed.

                  • [deletion_state_matching_frontier18] Above order seventeen every deletion state descends or reaches the fixed-endpoint matching frontier
                      STATEMENT
                      Let H be a minimum counterexample of order n>=18 and let H-x=P|Q be any one-vertex deletion two-cover. Let S|R|T be the canonical double-wrap spanning three-cover supplied by d26d8171978f, with S a Hamiltonian four-path. Then at least one of the following holds: (1) the pairwise-repartition component containing S|R|T contains a spanning three-cover of strictly smaller quadratic potential than S|R|T; (2) for one complementary path R=(r_1,...,r_m) of order m>=7, the endpoint six-set U=V(S) union {r_1,r_m} yields two Hamiltonian four-sets containing {r_1,r_m} and overlapping in three vertices, so d9a4b66724d2 gives a Hamiltonian five-set on their union or at least four Hamiltonian four-subsets of that union, all with non-Hamiltonian path-cover-two complements; (3) for such an R, V(S)=A disjoint-union B with |A|=|B|=2 and both A union {r_1,r_m} and B union {r_1,r_m} Hamiltonian with non-Hamiltonian path-cover-two complements. Thus the only no-descent residue not already amplified is the perfect matching on the four labels with both exterior endpoints fixed.
                      BODY / PROOF
                      Apply d26d8171978f to the deletion cover and obtain the canonical double-wrap three-cover S|R|T with |S|=4 and H-S=R|T. Since n>=18, |R|+|T|=n-4>=14, so after relabeling one complementary path R=(r_1,...,r_m) has m>=7. If either S union {r_1} or S union {r_m} is Hamiltonian, the corresponding endpoint transfer replaces pair sizes (4,m) by (5,m-1) and strictly decreases quadratic potential, giving (1). Assume both endpoint five-sets are non-Hamiltonian. Put U=V(S) union {r_1,r_m}. By two_bad_five_extensions_all_opposite01, U-{s} is Hamiltonian for every s in V(S). If U itself is Hamiltonian, repartition S|R as U | (r_2,...,r_{m-1}); the pair sizes change from (4,m) to (6,m-2), with quadratic-potential change 24-4m<0 because m>=7, again giving (1). Hence in the no-descent branch U is non-Hamiltonian, its two endpoint deletions are non-Hamiltonian, and all four S-label deletions are Hamiltonian. The theorem four_side_endpoint_matching_bridge01 applies. Its adjacent-edge branch gives exactly outcome (2), while its no-adjacent-edge branch says the graph defined by Hamiltonian two-vertex deletions is a perfect matching on V(S), yielding a partition V(S)=A disjoint-union B into two pairs for which A union {r_1,r_m} and B union {r_1,r_m} are Hamiltonian four-sets with non-Hamiltonian path-cover-two complements. This is outcome (3).

              • [deletion_state_mixed_gap_recomp01] Deletion-state double-wrap transport compresses directly to mixed support or a complete gap network
                  STATEMENT
                  Let H be a minimum counterexample of order n>=13 and let H-x=P|Q be any one-vertex deletion two-cover. Then there is a spanning three-cover S|R|T in the canonical double-wrap form, with S a Hamiltonian four-path, H-S=R|T a two-cover, and after relabelling m=|R|>=5. Put M equal to the displayed interior of R. At least one of the following holds. (1) One legal pairwise repartition of S|R has component orders (5,m-1) and quadratic-potential change 10-2m<=0; the move is neutral only for m=5 and strict for m>=6, hence whenever n>=15 it is strict if this alternative occurs. (2) H contains a proper Hamiltonian induced set U of order four or five meeting both S and V(M), with H-U non-Hamiltonian of path-cover number two; U may be chosen as one S-label plus three consecutive vertices of M, two S-labels plus three consecutive vertices of M, or two S-labels plus the two vertices of one displayed gap of M. (3) m>=7 and every s in S has a second-type failed-insertion obstruction at a distinct displayed gap g(s) of M. For every distinct s,t in S, adjacent gaps force the explicit cross triple of 36fccff06d48, while gaps at distance at least two yield the tight interval path joining s and t through the displayed subinterval between them. Thus every deletion state of order at least thirteen reaches, in one canonical argument, nonincreasing same-component transport, a genuinely mixed bounded Hamiltonian support, or the complete four-label gap network.
                  BODY / PROOF
                  Start from H-x=P|Q. By 8ededbb50716 together with 687bbaa431c3, the singleton lift of this deletion cover admits a canonical double-wrap rotation. Hence there is a spanning three-cover S|R|T with |S|=4, S Hamiltonian, H-S=R|T a two-cover, and both wrap failures positioned exactly as in the double-wrap construction. Relabel R,T so m=|R|>=|T|. Since n>=13, m+|T|=n-4>=9, so m>=5. Let M be R with its two displayed endpoints removed.\n\nApply the four-side endpoint package directly to S|R|T. If S together with one displayed endpoint of R is Hamiltonian, or if one of the synchronized residuals M+{s} is Hamiltonian, there is a legal pairwise repartition of S|R with orders (4,m)->(5,m-1). Its potential change is 25+(m-1)^2-(16+m^2)=10-2m. This proves (1), including neutrality only at m=5 and strictness for m>=6. If n>=15, then m+|T|>=11 and m>=|T| force m>=6.\n\nAssume no such move exists. Then the endpoint package gives, for every s in S, a Hamiltonian five-support F_s=(S-{s}) union {r_1,r_m} and a non-Hamiltonian residual M+{s}. Thus all four labels of S are noninsertable into the displayed path M. Apply the complete failed-insertion classification label by label. A first-type obstruction gives, by 0425e03e2aa3, either a Hamiltonian four-window consisting of one S-label and three consecutive vertices of M, or the exceptional cyclic non-Hamiltonian four-window whose extension by another S-label is a Hamiltonian five-set. Either way we obtain outcome (2), and the support meets both S and M. If two labels have second-type obstructions at the same gap, 36fccff06d48 gives a Hamiltonian four-set on those two labels and the two vertices of the gap, again outcome (2). In every such case the support is proper, so minimum-counterexample calculus gives a non-Hamiltonian path-cover-two complement.\n\nIt remains that all four labels have second-type obstructions at pairwise distinct gaps. Hence M contains at least five vertices and m>=7. Fix distinct s,t in S. If |g(s)-g(t)|>=2, the separated-gap clause of 36fccff06d48 gives the tight interval path joining s to t through the corresponding displayed subinterval of M. If |g(s)-g(t)|=1, its adjacent-gap clause gives either a Hamiltonian five-set on s,t and three consecutive vertices of M, which would be outcome (2), or the explicit adjacent-gap cross triple. Since we are in the no-(2) branch, the cross triple is forced. This proves the full pairwise network in (3).\n\nThe former order-15, order-14, order-13, and mixed-support nodes are therefore successive partial presentations of this single argument: the n-threshold arithmetic, the mixed-support strengthening, and the complete gap-network refinement are all internal steps of one theorem and no strength is lost by composing them.

                • [deletion_state_disturbance13] From order thirteen every deletion state reaches transport, mixed support, or a certified reversal/cycle disturbance
                    STATEMENT
                    Let H be a minimum counterexample of order n>=13 and let H-x=P|Q be any one-vertex deletion two-cover.
